data: All APIs live under https://api.mapx.at/v1/ and need a free API token from account.mapx.at. Send it as Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN or ?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN; see Access and limits. mx_pk_ tokens (public) work from allowed websites and Android apps with GET/HEAD, mx_sk_ tokens (secret) from servers. The pages below are generated from the OpenAPI description and always match the running service. Each page has a playground that calls the live API.
data.apis#APIs: Tiles Tileset list, TileJSON, XYZ tiles. Styles Styles, fonts, sprites, Static Tiles. Geocoding Forward, reverse and batch. Search Box Suggestions, retrieve, categories. Address Autofill and validation. Directions Routes, isochrone, matrix, matching, speed limits, corridor graph. Optimization Optimized trips and tour planning. Transit Journeys, stops, departures. Static Images Map images with overlays. Tilequery and Parcel Features and parcels at a point. Elevation Heights and profiles. Weather Observations, forecast, warnings, tiles. Air quality Index, pollutants, Saharan dust. Climate Solar potential, normals, snow, drought. Traffic Incidents, gantry speed limits, tiles.
data.conventions#Conventions: Coordinates are lon,lat (WGS84), several separated by ;. See Coordinates. Errors are application/problem+json (RFC 9457) with a stable code, including 401/403 for token problems. See Errors and limits. Limits are per token and zone (without a valid token per IP address); 429 carries Retry-After. See Access and limits. Caching: tiles, styles and TileJSON carry ETag; send If-None-Match to get 304. Versioning: the version is in the path. Fields do not change within a version, new ones are only added. Deprecations are announced in the Changelog with a sunset date.
data.more-reference#More reference: Tilesets: data sheets of every tileset. Style specification, Terrain-RGB, Tile scheme. Errors and limits, Migration, Changelog, Attribution. Status: health check of the API.

data.address-validation-free-text-or-structur:

Checks an address against the official register. status: match | corrected | ambiguous | not_found. Returns the normalized address, confidence (0 to 1), deviations[] per field (kind: spelling | wrong | added), coordinate, id and adrcd. Understands Str./Straße, abbreviations, umlauts and ß.

Daily air quality index and hourly nitrogen dioxide, ozone, PM10 and PM2.5 near the surface plus the Saharan dust load for a point, from the GeoSphere chemical weather model (3 km). data:
Climate of a point: yearly solar radiation and sunshine hours, temperature and precipitation normals with trend, hot and frost days, snow days per winter and the drought index. Source: GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0. The same object is properties.climate in the parcel dossier.
Base URL: https://api.mapx.at · Rate-limit zone: search (10/s) · Guide: Parcels
data.climate-at-a-point-solar-potential-norma:
GET /v1/climate/{coordinate}
Climate of one point from open data of GeoSphere Austria: solar potential (yearly global radiation in kWh/m2 and sunshine hours, mean of the last 3 complete years, 100 m), temperature and precipitation (normal 1991-2020, last 10 years, trend, monthly normals, 1 km), hot/summer/frost/ice days and tropical nights per year, snow days per winter and the current snow depth, and the drought index SPEI (90 and 365 days, latest value with class).
More Each section has source (dataset, cell, last day of data) and retrieved_at. Values are derived per grid cell and cached; the first request for a new cell fetches them from the source and can take 10 to 20 seconds (sections limits the work), later requests come from the cache. The same object is part of the parcel dossier (properties.climate). Outside Austria 404; 503 while the source is unavailable or rate limited. Data source: GeoSphere Austria (APOLIS, SPARTACUS, SNOWGRID-CL, WINFORE), CC BY 4.0 (attribution required).
Parameters

data:
Routing on the Austrian road graph (GIP.at). Profiles: driving, driving-traffic, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb, walking.
Base URL: https://api.mapx.at · Rate-limit zone: route (5/s), heavy (30/min) · Guide: Navigation
data.corridor-graph-for-offline-rerouting#Cor:
GET /v1/corridor-graph
Compact binary subgraph of the road network around a route, for recomputing a route without network (for example in a dead zone after a wrong turn). polyline is the route as polyline6 (e.g. routes[].geometry with geometries=polyline6), buffer the radius around it in meters (default 3000, at most 5000).
More The response body is a gzip stream (application/vnd.mapx.corridor-graph+gzip, no Content-Encoding) of a MXCG v1 file: a version header and the graph id of the server graph, nodes (microdegrees), directed arcs with travel time and weight in ms (the same values the router uses, so offline costs equal server costs), simplified link geometry, road name and reference, road class (FRC/FOW), maximum speed with a statutory flag, link flags (roundabout, ramp, toll, urban, motorway) and the turn restrictions between the arcs including derived U-turn bans. Arcs that cannot be driven are left out. Typically 1 to 3 MB per 100 km of route (compressed). Source: GIP.at (CC BY 4.0).
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description polyline query string yes – Route as polyline6 (at most 20,000 points) profile query string – driving (default), cycling or walking buffer query string 3000 Meters around the route, 100 to 5000, default 3000 Example
curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/corridor-graph?polyline=_wp~zAofsf%5C_nDouS_pR_af@&buffer=1000" -o result.bin const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/corridor-graph?polyline=_wp~zAofsf%5C_nDouS_pR_af@&buffer=1000", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } }); const blob = await res.blob(); import requests res = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/corridor-graph?polyline=_wp~zAofsf%5C_nDouS_pR_af@&buffer=1000", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}) open("result.bin", "wb").write(res.content) Example response: application/vnd.mapx.corridor-graph+gzip · Corridor graph (gzip of MXCG v1)

data.isochrones#Isochrones:
GET /v1/isochrone/{profile}/{coordinate}
Reachable areas, largest first; properties.contour/color/opacity. Zone heavy. Profile transit computes walking plus public transport (GTFS timetable, RAPTOR): walk to stops, ride from depart_at, walk on from every stop reached; only contours_minutes (default 5,10,15, at most 120 min), the timetable’s validity period applies (otherwise 422), metadata carries depart_at, transit_stops and attribution.
More access=foot|bike|car (default foot) chooses how the first stop is reached: bike = Bike & Ride (bike to any stop, +2 min for locking), car = Park & Ride (drive, at most 25 min, to stops with rail/metro/tram service, +3 min for parking, and to official GIP P+R sites, +2 min and a walk to the stop); the fastest combination wins, exit is always on foot. park=official restricts parking to official P+R/B+R sites. metadata then adds access, park, access_stops_improved and access_sites (top sites entries: source site|stop, kind, name, lon, lat, arrive_min, ready_min, stops_won). Bike carriage on trains is not in the timetable data, so there is no egress=bike. The other profiles reject depart_at, access and park (400).
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description profile path string yes – driving, driving-traffic, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb, walking or transit (walking plus public transport from depart_at); mapbox/ prefix allowed coordinate path string yes – lon,lat contours_minutes query string 5 Up to 4 values, comma-separated (default 5,10,15) contours_meters query string – Distances instead of minutes (not for transit) depart_at query string now Only transit: departure, ISO 8601 local time Europe/Vienna without offset (2026-11-10T08:00), or with Z/offset, or Unix seconds; default now access query string – Only transit: foot (default) | bike (Bike & Ride) | car (Park & Ride) park query string bike every stop Only transit with bike/car: any (default: bike every stop, car rail stops) | official (only official P+R/B+R sites) sites query string 10 Only transit with bike/car: number of access entries in metadata.access_sites (default 10, max 50) Example

data.routing#Routing:
GET /v1/directions/{profile}/{coordinates}
Trucks (driving-truck, over 3.5 t): vehicle size via weight, height, width, length, truck_type; roads are blocked per vehicle (weight-class, semi and trailer bans, height/width/weight/length limits). Truck speeds: at most 80 km/h on motorways, 70 on rural roads, 50 in built-up areas.
More District-wide bans (free-text ordinances) are not routed; affected roads appear as steps[].notices[] (type: truck_restriction). Responses add routes[].truck (the vehicle used) and routes[].toll.truck_go_km (kilometers subject to the GO toll; per step truck_go_m). 2 to 25 coordinates; legs are computed individually. Car routes (driving) contain routes[].toll (vignette and special-toll data), toll_road, toll_road_m and steps[].intersections[].classes; toll source ASFINAG, CC BY 4.0. From the GIP, steps additionally carry ref, destinations, milestone, maxspeed, ascent_m, descent_m and (cycling/walking) grade_pct, for cycling and cycling-mtb also bike_infrastructure (cycleway, lane, shared, none) and surface (paved, cobblestone, unpaved, offroad, unknown); routes[].summary has ascent, descent, max grade and elevation range. The default overview=simplified returns a simplified geometry, steps=true adds step geometry and intersections. Closures: driving and driving-traffic avoid binding full closures from the traffic reports (EVIS/ASFINAG) and list them in routes[].closures_avoided; driving without active closures along the route is unchanged. Navigation: steps=true with voice_instructions=true and/or banner_instructions=true adds Mapbox-style voice and banner instructions (all road profiles, texts in language). Speed limits: maxspeed (step and annotation) is {speed, unit, legal}; legal: true marks a statutory limit (5, 10, 20 … 130 km/h), legal: false a modeled GIP speed (e.g. 53, 84) that is not a limit; {unknown: true} without a value (backward compatible: speed and unit are unchanged). For limits along a corridor see /v1/speedlimits.
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description profile path string yes – driving, driving-traffic (with current traffic and closures), driving-truck (trucks over 3.5 t; vehicle size via weight/height/width/length/truck_type), cycling, cycling-mtb or walking (mapbox/ prefix allowed) coordinates path string yes – lon,lat;lon,lat;… steps query string – true for turn-by-turn steps (with maneuvers and intersections) geometries query string – geojson (default) | polyline | polyline6 overview query string – simplified (default, simplified route geometry), full (every vertex) or false (no geometry) language query string – de (default) or en alternatives query string – true (up to 2), false or 0 to 3; only with exactly 2 coordinates. Alternatives are built via laterally offset waypoints and appear as additional routes[] annotations query string – duration, distance, speed, maxspeed, elevation, weather_warnings (comma-separated; weather_warnings adds routes[].weather_warnings, the official warnings whose area the route crosses, without geometry): legs[].annotation per geometry segment; speed in m/s, maxspeed [{speed, unit: km/h, legal} | {unknown: true}] (driving only; legal is true for a statutory limit and false for a modeled speed such as 53 or 84 that must not be shown as a limit), elevation = mean segment height in m radiuses query string – Search radius per coordinate in meters, semicolon-separated, or unlimited approaches query string – unrestricted or curb per coordinate (validated, not yet used by the router) bearings query string – degrees,tolerance per coordinate (validated, not yet used by the router) incidents query string true for driving-traffic true/false: traffic incidents along the leg as legs[].incidents; default true for driving-traffic, otherwise false; cars only exclude query string – motorway, toll and/or ferry, comma-separated: motorway avoids motorways (category A; driving, driving-traffic, driving-truck); toll avoids all toll roads: vignette-required ASFINAG motorways and expressways (categories A and S) and special-toll sections (A9 Gleinalm/Bosruck, A10 Tauern/Katschberg, A11 Karawanken, A13 Brenner, S16 Arlberg; same profiles); ferry closes all ferry links (all profiles except driving-traffic, which returns 400). With ferry the route is computed without contraction hierarchies, so it takes some tens of milliseconds longer voice_instructions query string – true: steps[].voiceInstructions (Mapbox form with announcement and ssmlAnnouncement, language per language); requires steps=true; all road profiles (driving, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb, walking), with shorter announcement distances on foot (100 m, 40 m) and by bike (250 m, 80 m) banner_instructions query string – true: steps[].bannerInstructions (Mapbox form, primary/secondary with text and components; destination signage and road number); requires steps=true; all road profiles cycling_surface query string – any (default), cycling only; paved (close unpaved sections completely) is currently unavailable and returns 400 weight query string 40 driving-truck only: gross weight in t (default 40, 0.5 to 60); avoids weight-class bans and weight limits height query string 4 driving-truck only: vehicle height in m (default 4, 1.5 to 5); avoids height limits width query string 2 driving-truck only: vehicle width in m (default 2.55, 1 to 3.5) length query string – driving-truck only: vehicle length in m (2 to 40); length limits are only checked when given truck_type query semi | rigid | trailer – driving-truck only: semi (articulated lorry, default), rigid (lorry without trailer) or trailer (lorry with trailer) Example

data:
Every error is an application/problem+json document (RFC 9457). The type is a URI into this page: https://docs.mapx.at/api/errors/#. Branch on code (or type) and status, never on the text.
{ "type": "https://docs.mapx.at/api/errors/#invalid-parameter", "title": "Invalid parameter", "status": 400, "detail": "types: unknown value 'foo' (allowed: address, street, locality, place, district, region, postcode, poi)", "code": "invalid-parameter", "param": "types", "allowed": ["address", "street", "locality", "place", "district", "region", "postcode", "poi"] }
data.app-not-allowed#app-not-allowed:
403 · App not allowed
A public token bound to an Android app was used with a package name or signing certificate that does not match.
What to do: Send the headers X-Mapx-Android-Package and X-Mapx-Android-Cert of the registered app, or fix the binding in your account.
data.attribution#Attribution: JSON responses carrying data have a top-level attribution field (plain text, no HTML) naming the source to credit when displaying or passing on the data, e.g. Datenquelle: BEV – DKM, CC BY 4.0 for parcels or Datenquelle: GIP.at … for routing, matrix and isochrone. Exceptions: the lists /v1/styles, /v1/fonts, /v1/sprites (arrays); styles credit their sources in sources. See Attribution.
data.authentication-errors#Authentication err:
Every request needs a token (Access and limits). Authentication errors answer 401 or 403 as application/problem+json; the code is also in the response header X-Mapx-Reason (readable from browser scripts). Anonymous requests are still served during the transition period; they carry X-Mapx-Token-Warning: missing-token and will get 401 later.
# with an invalid or unknown token (here the placeholder itself) the answer is 401 invalid-token curl -si -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Melk" | head -12
data.bad-request#bad-request:
400 · Bad request
The request is invalid in a way no more specific code covers.
What to do: Read detail and fix the request.
data.caching#Caching: Header Value Cache-Control public, max-age=3600 (tiles, TileJSON, elevation, parcel), max-age=300 (geocoding, reverse, autofill suggestions, address validation via GET, tileset list), max-age=0 (routing, matrix, isochrone, POST requests) ETag, Last-Modified version; with If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since → 304 (tiles, styles, TileJSON, OpenAPI) Server-Timing router, search, render, total in milliseconds RateLimit-Policy zone and limit of the endpoint PMTiles files carry the release date in their name and never change; they may be cached indefinitely.

data.fields#Fields: Field Meaning type URI of the error type (anchor on this page) title Short summary of the type status HTTP status detail Explanation for this request; English by default code Stable machine-readable code, equals the anchor param Offending parameter (where applicable) allowed Accepted values for enumerations (where applicable)
data.internal-error#internal-error:
500 · Internal error
An unexpected error occurred on the server.
What to do: Retry once; if it persists, report the request.
data.invalid-body#invalid-body:
400 · Invalid request body
The body of a POST request is not valid JSON or not in the expected shape.
What to do: Check the JSON against the schema in the OpenAPI description.
data.invalid-coordinates#invalid-coordinates:
400 · Invalid coordinates
A coordinate (path segment or parameter) cannot be parsed or is outside the valid range. Unparsable path coordinates answer 400, not 404.
What to do: Send lon,lat in WGS84 degrees (longitude -180 to 180, latitude -90 to 90).
data.invalid-parameter#invalid-parameter:
400 · Invalid parameter
A parameter has a value that is malformed, out of range or not one of the accepted values. param names it; for enumerations allowed lists the accepted values.
What to do: Use a value from allowed or inside the range stated in detail.
data.invalid-token#invalid-token:
401 · Invalid token
The token is malformed or unknown (also after it was deleted or rotated).
What to do: Copy the token again from your account, check for a stray space or line break, and use the current token. Tokens start with mx_pk_ or mx_sk_.
data.ip-not-allowed#ip-not-allowed:
403 · IP address not allowed
The secret token is restricted to IP ranges and the request comes from another address.
What to do: Add the address (CIDR) to the token or send from an allowed host.
data.language#Language: title and detail are English by default. Send Accept-Language: de to get German texts; type, code, param and allowed stay identical. Responses carry Content-Language and Vary: Accept-Language. German detail is the generic description of the code; the English detail is the most specific.
data.method-not-allowed#method-not-allowed:
405 · Method not allowed
Only GET (and HEAD) is allowed, POST only for batch geocoding, optimization, address validation and traffic incidents.
What to do: Use the documented method.
data.missing-parameter#missing-parameter:
400 · Missing parameter
A required parameter is missing. param names it.
What to do: Add the parameter named in param.
data.missing-token#missing-token:
401 · Token missing
The request carries no token. Today anonymous requests are still answered during the transition period and carry the header X-Mapx-Token-Warning; afterwards they get this error.
What to do: Create a token at account.mapx.at and send it as Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN or ?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN. See Access and limits.
data.not-found#not-found:
404 · Not found
The addressed resource (a tile, a sprite, …) does not exist.
What to do: For tiles treat as an empty tile.
data.origin-missing#origin-missing:
403 · Origin missing
A public token was used without Origin and without Referer, so the site cannot be checked.
What to do: Call from a browser page, or use a secret token on a server.
data.origin-not-allowed#origin-not-allowed:
403 · Origin not allowed
A public token (mx_pk_) was used from a website whose Origin (or Referer host) is not in the allowed origins of the token.
What to do: Add the origin to the token (for development also localhost), or call the API from your server with a secret token.
data.pk-not-allowed#pk-not-allowed:
403 · Public token not allowed here
A public token only allows read access (GET, HEAD) to the public products.
What to do: Use a secret token (mx_sk_) from a server for this request.
data.rate-limited#rate-limited:
429 · Rate limit exceeded
Too many requests from your token (without a valid token: your IP address) in this endpoint group. See rate limits.
What to do: Wait Retry-After seconds, then retry with growing back-off. The RateLimit-Policy header of every response shows the zone.
data.rate-limits#Rate limits: Limits per token and zone are listed under Access and limits. Retry on 429 and 503 with growing delay and honor Retry-After; do not retry 400, 401, 403, 404 and 422 unchanged.
data.service-busy#service-busy:
503 · Service busy
The server is at its concurrency limit.
What to do: Wait Retry-After seconds and retry.
See also: Errors and limits for rate limits and caching.
data.service-unavailable#service-unavailable:
503 · Service unavailable
The data or service is temporarily unavailable (e.g. weather data not loaded yet, a style being rebuilt).
What to do: Retry later.
data.tile-out-of-range#tile-out-of-range:
404 · Tile out of range
The tile is outside the zoom or tile range of the tileset or style.
What to do: Stay within minzoom/maxzoom and bounds of the TileJSON.
data.token-blocked#token-blocked:
403 · Token blocked
The token was blocked in your account.
What to do: Unblock it in your account or use another token.
data.token-expired#token-expired:
401 · Token expired
The token is past its expiry date.
What to do: Create or rotate a token in your account.
data.unknown-font#unknown-font:
404 · Unknown font
The font name is not known.
What to do: List fonts with /v1/fonts.
data.unknown-id#unknown-id:
404 · Unknown id
A suggestion, address or place id is not known (or expired after a data update).
What to do: Search again and use the id from the fresh response.
data.unknown-parameter#unknown-parameter:
404 · Unknown parameter
A weather parameter name is not known.
What to do: Use one of temperature, precipitation, wind, humidity, cloud, pressure.
data.unknown-path#unknown-path:
404 · Unknown path
The path does not exist.
What to do: Check the path against the OpenAPI description. The former aliases /v1/{tileset}... and driving-ev were removed.
data.unknown-style#unknown-style:
404 · Unknown style
The style id is not known.
What to do: List styles with /v1/styles.
data.unknown-tileset#unknown-tileset:
404 · Unknown tileset
The tileset name is not known.
What to do: List tilesets with /v1/tiles.
data.unprocessable#unprocessable:
422 · Unprocessable request
The request is well-formed but cannot be answered, e.g. no route between the points or a date outside the timetable period.
What to do: Change the points or the time; read detail.
data.upstream-error#upstream-error:
502 · Upstream error
A backing service (search, router) did not answer or answered with an error.
What to do: Retry after a few seconds.

GET /v1/geocode
Search over the official address register, streets, places, municipalities, districts, postcodes and parcels. Road kilometers: B83 km 329,7, A1 km 41 or L190 km 3.5 (class A, S, B or L, number, the word km) return the point on the road at that kilometer as place_type road_ref with properties.road_ref (ref, km); the index holds a point every 0.1 km on motorways, expressways and federal roads and every 0.5 km on state roads (GIP.at), the nearest one is returned, the same state road number in several states gives several hits.
More Response: FeatureCollection with place_type, place_name, center, geometry, bbox. Always pass types for cheap queries.
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description q query string yes – Search text (also path form /v1/geocode/{q}.json) limit query integer (1–10) 5 1 to 10, default 5 types query string – Comma-separated result types: address, street, locality, place, district, region, postcode, poi, parcel (parcels only; input such as KG 14105 Gst 102/3, 14105/102/3, Landeck .102), road_ref (road kilometer; input such as B83 km 329,7, A1 km 41, L190 km 3.5) bbox query string – minlon,minlat,maxlon,maxlat proximity query string – lon,lat; ranks equal matches by distance Example

Since 2026-11-08 the API uses English identifiers for styles, tilesets, search categories and response fields. The former German names keep working unchanged until 2027-05-31 (sunset). After that they return 404, or the old fields are no longer included.
If nothing changes by 2027-05-31, requests with the old names will fail from then on. The new names already work today; switching is a pure rename, the data is identical.
data.fields#Fields: Endpoint old new /v1/parcel gstnr parcel_number /v1/parcel kgnr cadastral_municipality_id /v1/parcel bauflaeche is_building_land /v1/parcel quelle source /v1/elevation, /v1/elevation/profile, /v1/elevation/{coordinate}, /v1/tilequery stichtag reference_date Until the sunset, responses contain both fields. /v1/weather/* already returns wind direction as wind_direction_deg.
data.headers-on-old-names#Headers on old name:
A request using an old name returns the same response as with the new name, plus three headers:
Header Meaning Deprecation: @1794096000 The name has been deprecated since 2026-11-08 (RFC 9745, Unix timestamp in seconds). Sunset: Mon, 31 May 2027 00:00:00 GMT From this moment the old name is removed (RFC 8594). Link: ; rel="successor-version" The same resource under the new name. curl -sI -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/karte | grep -iE '^(deprecation|sunset|link)' The headers appear on styles (/v1/styles/{id} including sprites and static tiles), static images (/v1/static/{style}/…), tiles, TileJSON, tilequery, and on the Search Box when old category IDs are used. Responses with old field names (parcel, elevation) contain both names side by side; the old ones are marked deprecated in the OpenAPI.

Finds the best order of stops (traveling salesman) or plans tours for several vehicles with capacities and time windows.
Base URL: https://api.mapx.at · Rate-limit zone: heavy (30/min) · Guide: Navigation
data.optimized-order#Optimized order:
GET /v1/optimized-trips/{profile}/{coordinates}
2 to 25 coordinates. Exact up to 12 points, above that nearest neighbour with 2-opt and Or-opt over the duration matrix. Response like Directions: trips[] with one route, waypoints[] in input order with waypoint_index (position in the trip) and trips_index.
More Expensive: zone heavy.
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description profile path string yes – driving, driving-traffic (with current traffic and closures), driving-truck (trucks over 3.5 t; vehicle size via weight/height/width/length/truck_type), cycling, cycling-mtb or walking (mapbox/ prefix allowed) coordinates path string yes – lon,lat;lon,lat;… source query string – any (default) or first (point 0 is the start) destination query string – any (default) or last (last point is the end) roundtrip query string – true (default) returns to the start, or false; true with destination=last needs source=first steps query string – true for turn-by-turn steps geometries query string – geojson|polyline|polyline6 overview query string – simplified (default) | full | false language query string – de (default) or en Example

Renders a map image for a view and size, optionally with overlays. The result is cacheable (ETag).
Base URL: https://api.mapx.at · Rate-limit zone: heavy (30/min) · Guide: Static images
data.map-image-static-images-mapbox-form#Map:
GET /v1/static/{style}/{view}/{size}
satellite (BEV orthophoto, z5 to z18) or outdoors (hypsometric tints with hillshade from the DTM, z5 to z16). The streets* styles are rendered server-side from the style and the vector tiles (fills, lines, relief shading, place, road and water names; icons from the sprite, house numbers from z16; z0 to z22), usually under 0.2 s per 600x400.
More satellite-streets draws the orthophoto (z5 to z18) with roads, boundaries, contours, names and icons of the vector map on top. Output PNG (default) or WebP, at most 1280x1280 (2560x2560 pixels with @2x). Cache-Control and ETag (If-None-Match gives 304).
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description style path string yes – streets, streets-dawn, streets-dusk, streets-night, satellite, satellite-streets or outdoors (old ids karte, luftbild, … as deprecated alias) view path string yes – lon,lat,zoom[,bearing] (rotation in degrees, pitch only 0) or auto (only with overlays, fits the extent) size path string yes – {width}x{height}[@2x][.png|.webp], each 1 to 1280 Example
curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/satellite/16.3725,48.2085,15/600x400" -o result.png const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/satellite/16.3725,48.2085,15/600x400", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } }); const blob = await res.blob(); import requests res = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/satellite/16.3725,48.2085,15/600x400", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}) open("result.png", "wb").write(res.content) Example response: image/png, image/webp · Image

data.incident-reports-and-traffic-regulations:
GET /v1/traffic/incidents
Active reports (active=false: also ended and future), filterable by area, road (road, road_class), route, type and time window. Sorted by importance (closures and binding reports first, then motorways, expressways, federal and state roads, then start), paged with limit and cursor (total, next_cursor, next as relative URL, next_offset).

Each example runs live on the page, shows the complete code and a single HTML file to copy. The basis is MapLibre GL JS (4.7.1) with pmtiles (3.2.1), a free token and no build. The live maps use the docs token; in your copy replace YOUR_TOKEN with your own public token. Filter by product:
All (27)Maps (7)Search (5)Navigation (6)Elevation (3)Transit (2)Traffic (1)Static images (1)Parcels (1)Weather (2)SDK (2) Embed a map A map with the ready-made mapx style in an HTML page. Maps Switch the basemap Switch between map, aerial imagery and terrain. Maps Time of day and night mode The default style in four lighting moods. Maps 3D terrain Aerial imagery over the terrain model, tilted and exaggerated. Maps · Elevation Elevation on click A click queries the elevation at a point, terrain or surface. Elevation Elevation profile Click a line, see the profile. Elevation Search Search for places, addresses and peaks and fly to them. Search Route Click start and destination, get the way with length and duration. Navigation Weather overlay Temperature, precipitation or wind as an overlay, hour chosen with a slider. Weather Precipitation radar Rain and snow of the next three hours in 15-minute steps, played as an animation. Weather Reachability (isochrones) Which area can be reached in 5, 10 and 15 minutes? Navigation Travel-time matrix Travel times between several places in one request. Navigation Cadastre: parcel on click Parcel boundaries over aerial imagery, a click shows the number. Parcels TileJSON sources Add orthophoto and contours without a ready-made style. Maps 3D buildings Extruded buildings with BEV heights, camera tilted. Maps Search Box with suggestions Suggestions while typing, position after the click, type filter. Search Address autofill in a form Type a street, pick a suggestion, the form fills itself. Search Address validation Check an address against the official register and show the corrected result. Search Reverse geocoding Click the map, get the nearest address. Search Truck route with options Vehicle size, avoid tolls and motorways, alternatives. Navigation Tour planning Click stops, get the best order from the depot and back. Navigation Public transit route Click start and destination, get walking and riding legs. Transit Departures at a stop Click near a stop, see the next departures. Transit · SDK Traffic flow and incidents Traffic style plus the active incidents of the visible area. Traffic Static image for a listing Click a place, get a ready-made image URL with a pin. Static images Your own GeoJSON on the map Points, line and area over the mapx style, popup on click. Maps SDK: route planner and layers RouteControl with truck profile, LayerControl, search and style switcher. Navigation · SDK

data: Validation compares the four address parts with the BEV address register. The result has a status (match, corrected, ambiguous, not_found), the list of deviations and either the matching address with coordinates or a list of candidates. The pre-filled address has a typo on purpose. Validate Press Validate. The map needs JavaScript. Code // Address validation: check a typed address against the official register (BEV) and show the corrected result. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets', center: [13.8, 47.7], zoom: 6.5 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); const out = document.getElementById('ergebnis'); let marker; document.getElementById('pruefen').addEventListener('click', async () => { const p = new URLSearchParams(); for (const k of ['street', 'housenumber', 'postcode', 'place']) p.set(k, document.getElementById(k).value); try { const res = await fetch('https://api.mapx.at/v1/address/validate?' + p, AUTH); if (!res.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + res.status); const r = await res.json(); // status: match, corrected, ambiguous, not_found const hit = r.address ? { text: r.address, at: r.coordinates } : r.candidates?.[0] && { text: r.candidates[0].full_address, at: r.candidates[0].coordinates }; out.textContent = `Status: ${r.status}` + (r.deviations?.length ? `, deviations: ${r.deviations.map((d) => `${d.field} ${d.input} > ${d.expected}`).join('; ')}` : '') + (hit ? `, ${r.address ? 'address' : 'first candidate'}: ${hit.text}` : ''); marker?.remove(); if (hit) { marker = new maplibregl.Marker().setLngLat(hit.at).addTo(map); map.flyTo({ center: hit.at, zoom: 16 }); } } catch (e) { out.textContent = 'Error: ' + e.message; } }); Complete HTML file Save and open in a browser. Autofill is made for checkout and registration forms: one text field, one suggestion list, and the other fields (house number, postcode, place) are filled from the chosen suggestion. Each suggestion already carries its coordinates.
The map needs JavaScript. Code // Address autofill: type a street and number, pick a suggestion, the form fields fill themselves. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets', center: [13.8, 47.7], zoom: 6.5 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); const f = Object.fromEntries(['street', 'housenumber', 'postcode', 'place'].map((k) => [k, document.getElementById(k)])); const list = document.getElementById('treffer'); let marker; f.street.addEventListener('input', async () => { list.replaceChildren(); if (f.street.value.trim().length < 3) return; try { const res = await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/autofill/suggest?q=${encodeURIComponent(f.street.value)}&limit=5&session_token=demo`, AUTH); if (!res.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + res.status); for (const s of (await res.json()).suggestions) { const li = document.createElement('li'), b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = s.full_address; b.addEventListener('click', () => { for (const k of Object.keys(f)) f[k].value = s[k] ?? ''; marker?.remove(); marker = new maplibregl.Marker().setLngLat(s.coordinates).addTo(map); map.flyTo({ center: s.coordinates, zoom: 16 }); list.replaceChildren(); }); li.append(b); list.append(li); } } catch (e) { list.textContent = 'Error: ' + e.message; } }); Complete HTML file Save and open in a browser. All it needs is MapLibre GL JS 4.7.1 and pmtiles 3.2.1 from a CDN, plus your public token (replace YOUR_TOKEN), no build.

The streets style contains an extruded building layer that is switched off by default. The layer ids are listed in the style metadata (mapx:groups), so you switch a whole group on without knowing the names. Zoom in to level 15 or more and tilt the map (right mouse button or two fingers).
The map needs JavaScript. Code // 3D buildings: switch on the extruded building layer of the streets style and tilt the camera. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets', center: [16.3725, 48.2085], zoom: 16.2, pitch: 62, bearing: -20 }); // Stephansplatz, Vienna map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); map.on('style.load', () => { // The style lists its layer groups in the metadata, so no layer names are hard-coded. for (const id of map.getStyle().metadata['mapx:groups'].buildings3d) map.setLayoutProperty(id, 'visibility', 'visible'); }); Complete HTML file Save and open in a browser. All it needs is MapLibre GL JS 4.7.1 and pmtiles 3.2.1 from a CDN, plus your public token (replace YOUR_TOKEN), no build.

DeparturesPopup from the SDK finds the nearest stop to a click and lists the next departures from the scheduled timetable (no real-time data). The dots are the stops of the visible area from /v1/stops.
The map needs JavaScript. Code // Departures: click near a stop to see the next departures. Uses the DeparturesPopup of the mapx-gl SDK. import mapx from "https://map.mapx.at/sdk/v1/mapx-gl.bundle.js"; const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at const map = mapx.map({ accessToken: TOKEN, container: "map", style: "streets", center: [16.3725, 48.2085], zoom: 15.5 }); new mapx.DeparturesPopup(map, { limit: 8, radius: 150 }); // Show the stops of the visible area as dots. map.on("load", () => { map.addSource("stops", { type: "geojson", data: { type: "FeatureCollection", features: [] } }); map.addLayer({ id: "stops", type: "circle", source: "stops", paint: { "circle-radius": 6, "circle-color": "#2346d8", "circle-stroke-color": "#fff", "circle-stroke-width": 2 } }); const load = async () => { const b = map.getBounds(); const list = await mapx.stops({ bbox: [b.getWest(), b.getSouth(), b.getEast(), b.getNorth()], limit: 100 }); map.getSource("stops").setData({ type: "FeatureCollection", features: list.map((s) => ({ type: "Feature", properties: { name: s.name }, geometry: { type: "Point", coordinates: s.location } })) }); }; map.on("moveend", load); load(); }); Complete HTML file Save and open in a browser. All it needs is the mapx-gl SDK (it brings MapLibre GL JS 4.7.1 with) from a CDN, plus your public token (replace YOUR_TOKEN), no build.

The elevation API returns GeoJSON with elevation in metres. The DTM shows the terrain, the DSM buildings and vegetation.

Code // Query elevation: a click asks /v1/elevation (DTM or DSM) for the point. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/outdoors', center: [12.694, 47.074], zoom: 12 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); const popup = new maplibregl.Popup({ closeButton: false }); map.on('click', async (e) => { const modell = document.getElementById('modell').value; // dtm or dsm const url = `https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation?points=${e.lngLat.lng.toFixed(6)},${e.lngLat.lat.toFixed(6)}&model=${modell}`; try { const { features } = await (await fetch(url, AUTH)).json(); const h = features[0].properties.elevation; popup.setLngLat(e.lngLat).setText(h == null ? 'Outside the data' : `${h.toLocaleString('de-AT')} m (${modell.toUpperCase()})`).addTo(map); } catch (err) { popup.setLngLat(e.lngLat).setText('Error: ' + err.message).addTo(map); } }); Complete HTML file Save and open in a browser. The optimization API orders stops for one or more vehicles, with service times, capacities and time windows. Here one vehicle starts and ends in Melk. Click up to nine stops; every click plans again. The order is drawn with one directions request through all stops. Start over Click at least two stops. The map needs JavaScript. Code // Tour planning: click stops (up to 9), the optimization API finds the shortest order from the depot and back. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); // Note: POST needs a secret token (mx_sk_…), public tokens are read-only. Run this call from your server, not from a web page. const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const depot = [15.3294, 48.2272]; // Melk const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets', center: depot, zoom: 9 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); const stops = [], markers = []; let timer; new maplibregl.Marker({ color: '#222' }).setLngLat(depot).addTo(map); map.on('load', () => { map.addSource('tour', { type: 'geojson', data: { type: 'FeatureCollection', features: [] } }); map.addLayer({ id: 'tour', type: 'line', source: 'tour', layout: { 'line-cap': 'round', 'line-join': 'round' }, paint: { 'line-color': '#2346d8', 'line-width': 5 } }); }); map.on('click', (e) => { if (stops.length >= 9) return; stops.push([e.lngLat.lng, e.lngLat.lat]); markers.push(new maplibregl.Marker({ color: '#c8372d' }).setLngLat(e.lngLat).addTo(map)); clearTimeout(timer); // plan once after the last click if (stops.length >= 2) timer = setTimeout(plan, 600); }); document.getElementById('reset').addEventListener('click', () => { stops.length = 0; markers.splice(0).forEach((m) => m.remove()); map.getSource('tour').setData({ type: 'FeatureCollection', features: [] }); document.getElementById('info').textContent = 'Click at least two stops.'; }); async function plan() { const body = { vehicles: [{ id: 1, start: depot, end: depot }], services: stops.map((location, i) => ({ id: i + 1, location, service: 300 })) }; try { let res = await fetch('https://api.mapx.at/v1/optimization', { method: 'POST', headers: { ...AUTH.headers, 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(body) }); if (!res.ok) throw new Error((await res.json()).detail ?? The cadastre tileset contains boundary lines from zoom 16 with parcel number and cadastral municipality. queryRenderedFeatures reads them at the click point.
The map needs JavaScript. Code // Cadastre: a click on a parcel boundary shows the parcel number and cadastral municipality. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/satellite', center: [15.3306, 48.2275], zoom: 18 }); // Melk map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); map.on('load', () => { // Grenzlinien sichtbar machen (im Stil als Ebene "parcel", Quelle "kataster", ab Zoom 16) map.setLayoutProperty('parcel', 'visibility', 'visible'); }); map.on('click', (e) => { const box = [[e.point.x - 6, e.point.y - 6], [e.point.x + 6, e.point.y + 6]]; const f = map.queryRenderedFeatures(box, { layers: ['parcel'] })[0]; const text = f ? `Parcel ${f.properties.gstnr}, cadastral municipality ${f.properties.kgnr}` : 'No parcel boundary hit (visible from zoom 16).'; new maplibregl.Popup().setLngLat(e.lngLat).setText(text).addTo(map); }); Complete HTML file Save and open in a browser. data: The TileJSON /v1/weather/tiles/rr_nowcast.json lists the 15-minute steps under mapx:time.times. The example adds one raster layer per step and switches their visibility, so the animation does not wait for tiles. For a single point use GET /v1/weather/nowcast/{lon},{lat}. Code // Precipitation radar: nowcast tiles (15-minute steps, 3 hours) as an animation over the map. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const API = 'https://api.mapx.at/v1'; const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: API + '/styles/streets', center: [13.3, 47.6], zoom: 6.5 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); let times = [], timer = null; function zeigen(i) { const t = times[i]; document.getElementById('zeit').value = i; document.getElementById('info').textContent = `Radar-Nowcast ${t} (UTC), Quelle: GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0`; // one layer per time step, only the selected one is visible: tiles are already loaded when playing times.forEach((_, k) => map.setLayoutProperty('radar-' + k, 'visibility', k === i ? Reverse geocoding turns a coordinate into the nearest address, street or place. types limits the kind of result, radius the search distance in metres.
The map needs JavaScript. Code // Reverse geocoding: click the map, get the nearest address, street or place. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets', center: [16.3725, 48.2085], zoom: 15 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); const popup = new maplibregl.Popup({ closeButton: false }); map.on('click', async (e) => { const { lng, lat } = e.lngLat; try { const res = await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/reverse?lng=${lng}&lat=${lat}&limit=1&types=address,street,place`, AUTH); if (!res.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + res.status); const f = (await res.json()).features[0]; popup.setLngLat(e.lngLat).setText(f ? f.place_name : 'Nothing found nearby').addTo(map); } catch (err) { popup.setLngLat(e.lngLat).setText('Error: ' + err.message).addTo(map); } }); Complete HTML file Save and open in a browser. Search Box works in two steps: suggest returns suggestions while the user types, retrieve returns the position of the chosen one. Use the same session_token for both calls and a new one for the next search. The type filter limits the suggestions.
All typesAddressesStreetsPlacesPoints of interest The map needs JavaScript. Code // Search Box: suggestions while typing (suggest), position and details after the click (retrieve). One session token per search. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets', center: [14.3, 47.6], zoom: 7 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); const input = document.getElementById('q'), types = document.getElementById('types'), list = document.getElementById('treffer'); let marker, token = crypto.randomUUID(); input.addEventListener('input', async () => { list.replaceChildren(); if (input.value.trim().length < 2) return; const c = map.getCenter(); const url = `https://api.mapx.at/v1/searchbox/suggest?q=${encodeURIComponent(input.value)}&session_token=${token}&proximity=${c.lng},${c.lat}&limit=6` + (types.value ? `&types=${types.value}` : ''); try { const res = await fetch(url, AUTH); if (!res.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + res.status); for (const s of (await res.json()).suggestions) { const li = document.createElement('li'), b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = `${s.name} (${s.feature_type}) ${s.place_formatted ?? ''}`; b.addEventListener('click', () => pick(s.mapbox_id)); li.append(b); list.append(li); } } catch (e) { list.textContent = 'Error: ' + e.message; } }); async function pick(id) { const res = await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/searchbox/retrieve/${encodeURIComponent(id)}?session_token=${token}`, AUTH); const f = (await res.json()).features[0]; marker?.remove(); marker = new maplibregl.Marker().setLngLat(f.geometry.coordinates).addTo(map); map.flyTo({ center: f.geometry.coordinates, zoom: f.properties.zoom ?? 15 }); list.replaceChildren(); token = crypto.randomUUID(); // the session ends with retrieve } Complete HTML file Save and open in a browser. '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/traffic-day', center: [16.2, 48.1], zoom: 9 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); const list = document.getElementById('meldungen'); const popup = new maplibregl.Popup(); map.on('load', () => { map.addSource('incidents', { type: 'geojson', data: { type: 'FeatureCollection', features: [] } }); map.addLayer({ id: 'incidents', type: 'line', source: 'incidents', layout: { 'line-cap': 'round' }, paint: { 'line-color': ['case', ['get', 'closed'], '#c8372d', '#e8890c'], 'line-width': 6, 'line-opacity': 0.8 } }); map.on('click', 'incidents', (e) => popup.setLngLat(e.lngLat).setText(e.features[0].properties.text).addTo(map)); const load = async () => { const b = map.getBounds(); const res = await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?bbox=${b.getWest()},${b.getSouth()},${b.getEast()},${b.getNorth()}&active=true&limit=50`, AUTH); const fc = await res.json(); map.getSource('incidents').setData(fc); list.textContent = `${fc.features.length} active incident(s) in view` + (fc.features[0] ? `, e.g. ${fc.features[0].properties.road ?? data: The transit API combines walks on the road network with rides from the timetable. Without depart_at it plans for now; arrive_by plans backwards. Walking legs are drawn dashed, rides solid. Click the map for the start, then for the destination. The map needs JavaScript. Code // Public transit: click start and destination, get walking and riding legs for the next departure. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets', center: [16.3725, 48.2085], zoom: 12 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); const pts = [], markers = []; map.on('load', () => { map.addSource('legs', { type: 'geojson', data: { type: 'FeatureCollection', features: [] } }); const line = { 'line-width': 5 }; map.addLayer({ id: 'legs-ride', type: 'line', source: 'legs', filter: ['!=', ['get', 'mode'], 'walking'], layout: { 'line-cap': 'round', 'line-join': 'round' }, paint: { ...line, 'line-color': '#2346d8' } }); map.addLayer({ id: 'legs-walk', type: 'line', source: 'legs', filter: ['==', ['get', 'mode'], 'walking'], layout: { 'line-join': 'round' }, paint: { ...line, 'line-color': '#667', 'line-dasharray': [1, 1.5] } }); }); map.on('click', async (e) => { if (pts.length === 2) { pts.length = 0; markers.splice(0).forEach((m) => m.remove()); } pts.push([e.lngLat.lng, e.lngLat.lat]); markers.push(new maplibregl.Marker({ color: pts.length === 1 ? data:
Goal: A map where the orthophoto is draped over real terrain, shaded for depth and tiltable in the browser.
Prerequisites: a browser and any static web server (for example npx serve). A free API token (Access and limits).
This guide uses the DTM (elevation, type raster-dem) and the orthophoto (imagery, type raster). Both tilesets are added via TileJSON, so you never need a file name.
Create the page. A file index.html with MapLibre GL JS and a map container:
<meta charset="utf-8"> <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@4.7.1/dist/maplibre-gl.css"> <script src="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@4.7.1/dist/maplibre-gl.js">script> <style>html, body, #map { margin: 0; height: 100%; }style> <div id="map">div> Declare the sources. The elevation model as raster-dem, the orthophoto as raster:
const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // public token mx_pk_… // adds the token to every request to mapx.at (TileJSON and tiles) const withToken = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url }); const sources = { dem: { type: "raster-dem", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb.json", encoding: "mapbox" }, ortho: { type: "raster", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/orthophoto.json", tileSize: 512 } }; Stack the layers. Imagery at the bottom, hillshade on top with a light touch so the photo stays recognisable:
const layers = [ { id: "ortho", type: "raster", source: "ortho" }, { id: "hillshade", type: "hillshade", source: "dem", paint: { "hillshade-exaggeration": 0.4, "hillshade-shadow-color": "#000000" } } ]; Enable terrain. terrain lifts all layers to the DTM elevation. pitch tilts the view:
<script> const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: "map", transformRequest: withToken, center: [12.694, 47.074], zoom: 12, pitch: 65, bearing: 20, maxPitch: 80, style: { version: 8, sources: sources, layers: layers, terrain: { source: "dem", exaggeration: 1.3 } } }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl({ visualizePitch: true })); script> The constants from steps 2 and 3 (TOKEN, withToken, sources, layers) must appear in the same
data.next-steps#Next steps: Read the elevation at a click: map.queryTerrainElevation(e.lngLat), details in DTM terrain model. Contour lines and labels on top: Overlay contour lines. Elevation profile along a line: Elevation profile. Show the credit correctly: Attribution.
data.result#Result:
The aerial imagery lies on the terrain around the Großglockner, slopes are additionally shaded. The orthophoto reaches z18 (20 cm), the DTM z16 (1 m raster); MapLibre scales up automatically beyond that.
exaggeration exaggerates the relief. 1.0 is natural; for flat terrain 1.5 to 2 looks more plastic.

data:
Goal: Query an elevation profile (distance against elevation) for a route and draw it as a chart. Prerequisites: a browser. A free token, no framework, no library. With path and samples, the /v1/elevation endpoint returns elevation values spaced evenly by length along the line. Test the request. The line is made of lon,lat pairs separated by semicolons (longitude first). 50 sample points along a route at the Großglockner: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation?path=12.69,47.07;12.70,47.08&samples=50" The response is a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, one feature per sample with elevation (m) and distance_m (distance from the start). Create the page. A file profile.html with an empty SVG:

p> Load and draw the profile. The script fetches the data, scales distance and elevation to the canvas and builds a line with a filled area below:
data.next-steps#Next steps: All parameters and response fields: Elevation and profile. Line from a GPX track: join the coordinates as lon,lat;lon,lat, order see Coordinates. Limits for many requests: Errors and limits.
data.result#Result:
An SVG chart with area and line of elevation over distance, with length, ascent and descent below.
More samples give a finer ascent and descent but also more noise. With model=dsm the profile follows the surface (trees, buildings) instead of the ground, see DTM and DSM. A path has 2 to 512 vertices, samples 2 to 1024.

data: mapx has two height models of 1 m resolution (BEV, laser scanning): the terrain model dtm (bare ground) and the surface model dsm (including trees and buildings). Use dtm for gradients, profiles and trails, dsm for visibility and building heights. Every request needs a token (Access and limits); curl samples send it as a header, browser samples as access_token.
data.3d-terrain-in-the-map#3D terrain in the:
Add the terrain-rgb tileset as raster-dem source and turn on terrain:
map.on("load", () => { map.addSource("dem", { type: "raster-dem", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb.json", tileSize: 512 }); map.setTerrain({ source: "dem", exaggeration: 1.2 }); map.addLayer({ id: "hillshade", type: "hillshade", source: "dem" }); }); map.setPitch(60); Step-by-step with aerial imagery: 3D terrain with orthophoto. The style outdoors already includes hillshade and contours.
data.elevation-profile#Elevation profile: const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation/profile?coordinates=12.69,47.07;12.72,47.09&samples=50&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"; const { properties: p } = await (await fetch(url)).json(); console.log(p.ascent_m, p.descent_m, p.min_m, p.max_m); // p.distances[i] (m from the start) and p.elevations[i] (m) are ready for a chart Up to 1024 samples along a line of 2 to 512 vertices. Example with a chart: Elevation profile. Routes already carry ascent and descent in routes[].summary; use annotations=elevation for a height per segment.
data.height-at-a-point#Height at a point:
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation/12.694,47.074" | jq '.properties | {dtm, dsm}' Several points, up to 512, in one request:
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation?points=12.694,47.074;15.3294,48.2272&model=dtm&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"; const { features } = await (await fetch(url)).json(); console.log(features.map((f) => f.properties.elevation)); // meters above sea level Heights are in meters with 0.1 m steps. Outside the data area the value is null.

data.read-heights-from-tiles#Read heights fro: The tiles use the Terrain-RGB encoding: height = -10000 + (R * 65536 + G * 256 + B) * 0.1. Decode tiles yourself for bulk work, see Terrain-RGB. For single points the API is simpler.
