mapx delivers maps as ready-made styles and as tiles. Use a style to get a complete map in one line; use tilesets when you build your own style.
Before you start: a page with MapLibre GL JS, see First map. You need a free token (Access and limits); the snippets show YOUR_TOKEN only where it matters. The map options below assume the transformRequest from First map, which adds the token to every request to mapx.at.
data.add-tilesets-to-your-own-style#Add tiles:
Every tileset has a TileJSON address https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/{tileset}.json. MapLibre reads zoom range, bounds and attribution from it.
Tileset Type Content streets vector Roads, rail, water, boundaries, places, buildings cadastre vector Parcel boundaries (z16) contours vector Contour lines terrain-rgb, dsm raster-dem Terrain and surface height orthophoto raster Aerial photo, up to z18 map.on("load", () => { map.addSource("cadastre", { type: "vector", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/cadastre.json" }); map.addLayer({ id: "parcels", type: "line", source: "cadastre", "source-layer": "parcel_l", paint: { "line-color": "#e11d48", "line-width": 1 } }); }); Layer names and fields: Tilesets. Add your own data the same way with a geojson source.
data.next#Next: Style the basemap Tilesets Styles API and Tiles API
data.offline-and-bulk-use#Offline and bulk us:
Each tileset is also one PMTiles file. Download it once instead of fetching tiles: Self-host PMTiles.
Show the data source on the map. MapLibre does this automatically when you load a style or TileJSON, see Attribution.
data.other-clients#Other clients:
The style and TileJSON formats work in MapLibre, Mapbox GL JS clients that accept custom URLs, Leaflet with a vector plugin, OpenLayers and QGIS. For clients without vector support, Static Tiles deliver the rendered style as raster tiles:
https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets/tiles/512/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN
data.use-a-style#Use a style: Style Look streets Base map, roads, places, buildings streets-dawn, streets-dusk, streets-night The same map in other light satellite Orthophoto satellite-streets Orthophoto with roads and labels outdoors Contours, hillshade, trails const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: "map", style: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/outdoors", transformRequest: withToken, // from First map: adds the token to every mapx.at request center: [12.694, 47.074], zoom: 12, // Grossglockner }); Switching style at runtime replaces layers and sources: call map.setStyle(url). See Switch the basemap.
data.weather-and-traffic-overlays#Weather and:
Raster weather tiles have a time dimension; the TileJSON of temperature, precipitation, wind, humidity, cloud or pressure lists the available times. The same URL scheme serves the air quality layers aqi (daily index), no2, o3, pm10, pm25 and dust (Saharan dust), see Air Quality API. Official weather warnings are GeoJSON (/v1/weather/warnings, add it as a geojson source and colour by level).
map.addSource("temp", { type: "raster", url: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/weather/tiles/temperature.json", tileSize: 256 }); map.addLayer({ id: "temp", type: "raster", source: "temp", paint: { "raster-opacity": 0.6 } }); The traffic layer is a vector source, see Traffic. Example: Weather overlay.

data:
Routing runs on the Austrian road graph (GIP.at). Coordinates are lon,lat, joined with ;. Every request needs a token (Access and limits); curl samples send it as a header, browser samples as access_token.
Task Endpoint Zone Route between 2 to 25 points /v1/directions/{profile}/{coordinates} route Area reachable in N minutes /v1/isochrone/{profile}/{coordinate} heavy Travel times between many points /v1/matrix/{profile}/{coordinates} heavy Snap a GPS trace to roads /v1/matching/{profile}/{coordinates} heavy Best order of stops /v1/optimized-trips/{profile}/{coordinates} heavy Tours for several vehicles POST /v1/optimization heavy
data.a-route#A route: const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.3294,48.2272?steps=true&language=en&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"; const { routes } = await (await fetch(url)).json(); const r = routes[0]; console.log(r.distance, "m", r.duration, "s"); overview=simplified (default) returns a light geometry, full every vertex, false none. steps=true adds turn-by-turn steps. alternatives=true adds up to two more routes[]. annotations=duration,distance,speed,maxspeed,elevation adds values per segment. With cycling_surface=any (default) unpaved sections are rated worse but stay allowed. Heights inside bridges and tunnels are not taken from the terrain model. maxspeed (step and annotation) is {speed, unit, legal}: legal: true marks a statutory limit (5, 10, 20 … 130 km/h), legal: false a modeled GIP speed such as 53 or 84 km/h, which is a routing speed and not a limit and must not be shown as a speed sign. {unknown: true} means no value (many motorways). Existing clients that only read speed and unit keep working. Cycling and walking steps carry grade_pct; the route summary has ascent, descent and elevation range.
data.closures#Closures:
Binding full closures from the traffic reports (EVIS/ASFINAG) are avoided by driving and driving-traffic. The roads concerned are blocked for the route search; routes[].closures_avoided lists the closures that the route without closures would have driven through (id, text, road, category). If a closure cannot be avoided, the route runs through it and routes[].closures_unavoidable lists it. Conditional closures (weekdays, hours in the text) only discourage a road and are not listed. Source: ASFINAG, CC BY 4.0; show the texts unchanged.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/14.2,48.27;14.45,48.30?overview=false" | jq '.routes[0].closures_avoided'
data.handle-failures#Handle failures: 422 means the request is valid but unanswerable, for example no route between the points. 400 carries the faulty parameter in param. Retry 429 after Retry-After seconds. See Errors and limits.
data.isochrones-matrix-matching#Isochrones, m: // Where can I walk in 5, 10 and 15 minutes? const iso = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/isochrone/walking/16.3725,48.2085?contours_minutes=5,10,15&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN")).json(); // Travel times from the first point to the others const m = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/matrix/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.3294,48.2272;14.2858,48.3069?sources=0&annotations=duration,distance&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN")).json(); The isochrone result is a FeatureCollection of polygons, largest first. Show it with a fill layer; see Isochrone and Matrix. Map matching takes a GPS trace and returns the matched route.
data.next#Next: Directions API, Optimization API Traffic: incidents along a route Route example
data.offline-rerouting#Offline rerouting:
GET /v1/corridor-graph returns the road network around a route as one compact binary file (gzip stream, application/vnd.mapx.corridor-graph+gzip), so an app can recompute a route without network, for example after a wrong turn in a dead zone. Pass the route as polyline6 in polyline, the radius in buffer (100 to 5000 m, default 3000) and profile (driving default, cycling or walking). The file holds nodes, arcs with the travel times the router uses, road names, speed limits and turn restrictions; expect 1 to 3 MB per 100 km of route. Zone heavy. Source: GIP.at, CC BY 4.0.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -G "https://api.mapx.at/v1/corridor-graph" --data-urlencode "polyline@route.txt" -d buffer=500 -o corridor.mxcg
data.profiles#Profiles: Profile For driving Car driving-traffic Car with current traffic and closures driving-truck Trucks over 3.5 t cycling Bike: prefers cycle paths, lanes and signposted routes, rates unpaved sections and steep grades worse cycling-mtb Mountain bike: prefers forest tracks and singletrails, considers the MTB difficulty walking On foot Public transport is a separate API: Transit.
data.speed-limits-along-a-route#Speed limits:
GET /v1/speedlimits returns the statutory limits of the road network as compact GeoJSON, either in a box (bbox, at most 0.08 square degrees, about 28 by 28 km) or in a corridor around a route (corridor as polyline6 plus buffer in meters, default 30). Each road link is a LineString (digitizing direction) with limit_kmh, direction (both, forward, backward) and id. Links without a statutory limit are left out, so the sign display never shows a modeled speed.
# route as polyline6, then the limits in a 30 m corridor curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/speedlimits?bbox=15.325,48.225,15.335,48.23" | jq '.features | length' curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/15.6256,48.2049;15.3294,48.2272?geometries=polyline6&overview=full" | jq -j '.routes[0].geometry' > route.txt curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -G "https://api.mapx.at/v1/speedlimits" --data-urlencode "corridor@route.txt" -d buffer=30 | jq '.features | length' Write the polyline without a trailing newline (jq -j). Long routes can exceed the URL length of a GET request; split them into sections of about 500 points. Source: GIP.at, CC BY 4.0.
data.tolls#Tolls:
Car routes include toll_road, toll_road_m and toll with vignette products and special toll sections. Truck routes report the kilometers subject to the GO toll in routes[].toll.truck_go_km. Avoid tolls or motorways:
.../directions/driving/{coordinates}?exclude=toll .../directions/driving/{coordinates}?exclude=motorway,toll Vignette roads remain allowed with exclude=toll. Toll source: ASFINAG, CC BY 4.0.
exclude=motorway and exclude=toll work for driving, driving-traffic and driving-truck.
exclude=ferry closes all ferry links and works for every profile (driving, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb, walking) alone or combined, e.g. exclude=toll,ferry; driving-traffic returns 400. Because this variant is computed without contraction hierarchies, the response takes some tens of milliseconds longer. If a destination can only be reached by ferry (an island, for example), the request returns no route.
data.tour-planning#Tour planning:
optimized-trips orders up to 25 stops (round trip or fixed start and end). POST /v1/optimization plans tours for several vehicles with capacities and time windows.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -X POST https://api.mapx.at/v1/optimization -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "vehicles": [{ "id": 1, "start": [16.3725, 48.2083], "end": [16.3725, 48.2083] }], "services": [{ "id": 1, "location": [15.6256, 48.2049], "service": 300 }, { "id": 2, "location": [14.2858, 48.3069], "service": 300 }] }' | jq '.summary'
data.truck-routes#Truck routes: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving-truck/15.6256,48.2049;15.3294,48.2272?weight=40&height=4&width=2.55&length=16.5&truck_type=semi&overview=false" | jq '.routes[0] | {distance, duration, truck}' The router avoids roads closed to the vehicle: weight-class and trailer bans, height, width, weight and length limits. Speeds are capped at 80 km/h on motorways, 70 on rural roads, 50 in built-up areas. District-wide bans from free-text ordinances are not routed; affected roads are reported in steps[].notices[] with type: truck_restriction.
data.voice-and-banner-instructions#Voice and:
With steps=true you can add voice_instructions=true and banner_instructions=true (all road profiles: driving, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb and walking). The format follows Mapbox: each step carries the instructions for the maneuver at its end.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/15.6256,48.2049;15.3294,48.2272?steps=true&voice_instructions=true&banner_instructions=true&language=en&overview=false" | jq '.routes[0].legs[0].steps[1] | {voiceInstructions, bannerInstructions}' voiceInstructions[]: distanceAlongGeometry (meters before the end of the step at which to speak), announcement and ssmlAnnouncement. Announcement distances depend on speed: on motorways 2 km, 1 km and 300 m ahead, on rural roads 1 km, 400 m and 120 m, in town 400 m and 150 m; the last one is spoken without a distance. On foot the announcements come 100 m and 40 m ahead, by bike 250 m and 80 m ahead. The texts follow language (de or en) for every profile. The first step also announces the departure. language=de|en selects the language. bannerInstructions[]: primary and optional secondary with text, components[] (type icon for the road number, text for names and destination signage), type, modifier. With destination signage, the destination is the primary text and the road the secondary line.

data:
Goal: Place contour lines of suitable density over aerial imagery, draw index lines more strongly and label them with their elevation.
Prerequisites: a browser, a static web server and a free public token (Access and limits). Labels use the mapx fonts, see Style the basemap.
The contour lines tileset has a layer contour_l with the fields ele (elevation in m), index (1 = index line) and lvl (generalisation level 10, 12, 14, 16). Lines exist from z10.
Page with background. The orthophoto as base, the contours as a vector source:
<meta charset="utf-8"> <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@4.7.1/dist/maplibre-gl.css"> <script src="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@4.7.1/dist/maplibre-gl.js">script> <style>html, body, #map { margin: 0; height: 100%; }style> <div id="map">div> <script> const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // public token mx_pk_… // adds the token to every request to mapx.at (TileJSON, tiles, fonts) const withToken = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url }); const sources = { ortho: { type: "raster", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/orthophoto.json", tileSize: 512 }, contours: { type: "vector", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/contours.json" } }; Pick the level. The tiles contain several levels with their own line interval. To show only the matching level per zoom, filter by lvl:
Zoom lvl Interval Index line 10–11 10 100 m 500 m 12–13 12 50 m 200 m 14–15 14 20 m 100 m from 16 16 10 m 50 m One layer per level, limited with minzoom and maxzoom:
const levels = [ { lvl: 10, min: 10, max: 12 }, { lvl: 12, min: 12, max: 14 }, { lvl: 14, min: 14, max: 16 }, { lvl: 16, min: 16, max: 24 } ]; const lineLayers = levels.flatMap(({ lvl, min, max }) => [ { id: `line-${lvl}`, type: "line", source: "contours", "source-layer": "contour_l", minzoom: min, maxzoom: max, filter: ["all", ["==", ["get", "lvl"], lvl], ["!=", ["get", "index"], 1]], paint: { "line-color": "#ffd9a0", "line-width": 0.6, "line-opacity": 0.8 } }, { id: `index-${lvl}`, type: "line", source: "contours", "source-layer": "contour_l", minzoom: min, maxzoom: max, filter: ["all", ["==", ["get", "lvl"], lvl], ["==", ["get", "index"], 1]], paint: { "line-color": "#ffb347", "line-width": 1.4 } } ]); Elevation labels. Only index lines carry a number. symbol-placement: "line" runs the text along the line:
const labels = { id: "ele-text", type: "symbol", source: "contours", "source-layer": "contour_l", minzoom: 12, filter: ["==", ["get", "index"], 1], layout: { "symbol-placement": "line", "text-field": ["concat", ["to-string", ["get", "ele"]], " m"], "text-font": ["Open Sans Semibold"], "text-size": 11 }, paint: { "text-color": "#fff", "text-halo-color": "#7a4a00", "text-halo-width": 1.5 } }; text-font must be a font that /v1/fonts lists (GET /v1/fonts), for example Open Sans Semibold or Noto Sans Regular.
Start the map.
new maplibregl.Map({ container: "map", transformRequest: withToken, center: [12.694, 47.074], zoom: 14, style: { version: 8, glyphs: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf", sources: sources, layers: [{ id: "ortho", type: "raster", source: "ortho" }, ...lineLayers, labels] } }); </script>
data.next-steps#Next steps: Fields and levels in detail: Contour lines. Three-dimensional terrain: 3D terrain. Credits: Attribution.
data.result#Result:
Fine contour lines lie over the aerial imagery, their interval follows the zoom (100 m to 10 m). Index lines are strong and carry the elevation in metres.
For a map instead of imagery, replace the orthophoto layer with the layers from Style the basemap; put the contours on top.
Without a filter on lvl, several levels overlap when the map overzooms. Lines end below z10; for smaller scales the relief stays visible through hillshading.

data:
The cadastre (BEV, DKM) is available as a vector tileset for drawing and as an API for the parcel at a point. The data is for orientation and not legally binding. Every request needs a token (Access and limits); curl samples send it as a header, browser samples as access_token.
Task Use Draw parcel boundaries tileset cadastre (z16) Parcel number, area and cadastral municipality at a point /v1/parcel/{lon},{lat} Query any vector tileset at a point /v1/tilequery/{tilesets}/{lon},{lat}.json Search for a parcel Geocoding: parcels are among the searched objects
data.click-a-parcel-on-the-map#Click a parcel:
map.on("load", () => { map.addSource("cadastre", { type: "vector", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/cadastre.json" }); map.addLayer({ id: "parcel-lines", type: "line", source: "cadastre", "source-layer": "parcel_l", paint: { "line-color": "#e11d48" } }); }); map.on("click", async (e) => { const { lng, lat } = e.lngLat; const res = await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/parcel/${lng},${lat}?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`); const [parcel] = (await res.json()).features; if (!parcel) return; const p = parcel.properties; new maplibregl.Popup().setLngLat(e.lngLat) .setHTML(`Parcel ${p.parcel_number}
${Math.round(p.area_m2)} m²`).addTo(map); }); Full example: Parcel on click. The cadastral municipality (cadastral_municipality_id) is part of the identity of a parcel: the number alone is not unique.
data.next#Next: Tilequery and Parcel API Tilesets: layers and fields of the cadastre Elevation: height of the parcel
data.parcel-at-a-point#Parcel at a point: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/parcel/15.3294,48.2272" | jq '.features[0].properties | {parcel_number, cadastral_municipality_id, area_m2, is_building_land}' The result is a FeatureCollection with the parcel polygon. The area is computed from the boundary lines and deviates from the register value by per mille. A building returns its building parcel; the number then starts with a dot. Parcels that extend beyond the 2 km tile window around the point are missing, and the list is empty outside the cadastre data.
data.parcel-dossier#Parcel dossier:
GET /v1/parcels/{id} returns everything the open data say about one parcel in one call, for all roughly 10.2 million parcels of Austria (DKM key date in reference_date). The ID is - with / written as _, building parcels with a leading dot (14143-473_1, 14143-.98); it is properties.parcel_id in search results and in the point query.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/parcels/14143-473_1" | jq '.properties | {area_m2, land_use, buildings: .buildings.count, elevation, nearest_transit_stop}' Field Content cadastral_municipality, municipality, district, state {id, name} area_m2, area_ellipsoidal_m2 area in the Gauss-Krueger plane (as the cadastre computes it) and on the ellipsoid; the register value is not part of the open data land_use DKM land use classes with area_m2 and share buildings count, footprint, heights from BEV DLM where available, the 25 largest elevation min, mean, max and mean/max slope from the terrain model on a point grid inside the parcel addresses, nearest_transit_stop register addresses on the parcel, nearest stop within 2 km orthophoto flight year and date climate solar potential, temperature and precipitation normals, hot and snow days, drought index; same object as /v1/climate/{lon},{lat} at the parcel’s inner point. While a new area is being loaded, sections are null with status: "partial"; ask again after retry_after_s seconds links.static_image ready-made static image URL with the parcel outlined The point query adds parcel_id and links.dossier; ?include=dossier returns the full dossier per feature. Reference: Tilequery and Parcel API.
data.parcel-image-for-a-listing#Parcel image:
Combine the parcel with a static image using the polygon as GeoJSON overlay:
const parcel = (await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/parcel/15.3294,48.2272?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN")).json()).features[0]; const overlay = encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({ type: "Feature", properties: { stroke: "#e11d48", "stroke-width": 3, fill: "#e11d48", "fill-opacity": 0.2 }, geometry: parcel.geometry })); const img = `https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/satellite/geojson(${overlay})/auto/800x500.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`;
data.parcel-search#Parcel search:
Geocoding and Search Box know types=parcel for all cadastral municipalities:
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=KG+14143+Gst+288/4&types=parcel" # exact hit curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=14143/288/4&types=parcel" curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Melk+.98&types=parcel" # building parcel KG 14143 Gst 288/4, 14143/288/4 and 14143 288/4 are unambiguous (a five-digit number next to a parcel number is the KG number, postcodes have four digits). Melk 288/4 puts hits with that number first.
data.tilequery#Tilequery:
Tilequery reads the vector tile at the highest zoom and returns the features nearest to the point (radius up to 2000 m).
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/tilequery/cadastre/15.3294,48.2272.json?radius=30&limit=3" | jq '.features[].properties.tilequery' Combine tilesets with a comma, for example streets,cadastre. Each feature has tilequery.distance (m), geometry and layer.

data:
Goal: Use mapx orthophoto, elevation models and vector data as layers in QGIS, without a download. You need a free token (Access and limits); append ?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN to every layer URL. Use a secret token (mx_sk_…) on your own computer: a public token only works for its allowed origins, and QGIS is not a website.
Prerequisites: QGIS 3.x (3.32 or newer for direct PMTiles).
data.dtm-and-dsm#DTM and DSM:
The elevation tiles are Terrain-RGB: the elevation is stored in the colour channels. Use the same kind of connection with the URL
https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN (max. zoom 16; use dsm instead of terrain-rgb for the surface model). The layer first shows the encoded colour. Get the elevation in the Raster Calculator from the three bands:
-10000 + ("Layer@1" * 65536 + "Layer@2" * 256 + "Layer@3") * 0.1 (replace Layer with the name of your layer). The result is the elevation in metres; from it you can derive slope, aspect and hillshade.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Understand the elevation model: Terrain-RGB. Keep data locally: Self-host PMTiles. Credits in maps and reports: Attribution.
data.orthophoto-as-an-xyz-layer#Orthophoto as:
In the Browser panel, right-click XYZ Tiles, New Connection.
Name mapx Orthophoto, URL:
https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/orthophoto/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN Min. Zoom Level 5, Max. Zoom Level 18, Tile Resolution 512 (Mapbox style, 512 px). Leave Referer and Authentication empty; the token in the URL is enough.
Save with OK and load the connection into the map by double-click.
The project CRS can be anything, QGIS reprojects the Web Mercator tiles.
data.pmtiles-directly-qgis-332-and-newer#PMTi:
Vector tilesets can also be opened directly as a PMTiles file from QGIS 3.32, locally or over HTTP. The file name with its cut-off date is on each product page under key figures.
Browser panel, right-click Vector Tiles, New Generic Connection. Set the Service type to PMTiles (or pick a local file) and enter the file as URL: https://tiles.mapx.at/.pmtiles?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN. Save with OK and load it into the map. QGIS reads only the required tiles via HTTP range. Imagery and elevation tiles (orthophoto, DTM, DSM) are added through the XYZ connection above.
If your QGIS version does not offer the PMTiles service type, use the vector tile connection above; it delivers the same tiles.
data.vector-tiles#Vector tiles:
Browser panel, right-click Vector Tiles, New Generic Connection.
Name mapx Basemap, URL:
https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/streets/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN Enter Min. Zoom Level 0, Max. Zoom Level 16, OK.
Drag the connection into the map. QGIS first shows a default style; change the look in the layer style editor or with your own style.
The same procedure works for contours (max 16, min 10), cadastre (zoom 16) and orthophoto-flight-blocks (zoom 6 to 17). All tilesets: Tiles.

data: mapx-gl is a small add-on (ESM, TypeScript) for MapLibre GL JS. It sets the style URLs, registers the pmtiles:// protocol, wraps the APIs in typed functions and adds ready-made controls. Peer dependencies: maplibre-gl@{V.maplibre} and pmtiles@{V.pmtiles}.
data.install#Install:
Load the bundle from https://map.mapx.at/sdk/v1/ (CORS is open) or download the files and serve them with your page:
File Use mapx-gl.bundle.js Everything included, load as
data.map#Map: mapx.map(options) returns a MapLibre map. accessToken is your public token (Access and limits); it applies to the map and to all helpers. Without a map, call mapx.setAccessToken("YOUR_TOKEN") once. style is a short name (streets, streets-dawn, streets-dusk, streets-night, satellite, outdoors) that becomes https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/{id}, or any style URL or object. terrain: true turns on 3D terrain.

data: Controls are added with map.addControl(control, position). Popups attach to the map with new Popup(map, options). Texts are German when the page language or browser is German, otherwise English.
data.combine-popups-and-tools#Combine popups:
Both popups react to every map click. When you use them together with RouteControl, MeasureControl or another click tool, create them on demand and call remove() while the tool is active:
let parcels = new mapx.ParcelPopup(map); document.querySelector("#tools").onchange = (e) => (e.target.checked ? parcels.remove() : (parcels = new mapx.ParcelPopup(map)));
data.departurespopup#DeparturesPopup:
A click finds the nearest stop within radius metres and lists the next departures of the scheduled timetable.
const departures = new mapx.DeparturesPopup(map, { limit: 8, radius: 150 }); departures.open("at:49:1320"); // or by stop id, or [lng, lat] Live example.
data.layercontrol#LayerControl:
Switches whole layer groups on and off. The groups come from the style metadata (mapx:groups), so it works with every mapx style and shows new groups without a code change. Overlays from mapx:overlays (for example traffic) are offered as well when you do not restrict groups.
map.addControl(new mapx.LayerControl({ groups: ["buildings", "parcels", "relief", "bike_routes"], labels: { bike_routes: "Cycle routes", relief: "Hillshade and contours" }, }), "top-right");

data.parcelpopup#ParcelPopup:
A click shows the parcel at that point: number, area, cadastral municipality, and with dossier: true (default) buildings and elevation range. The outline is highlighted.
new mapx.ParcelPopup(map, { dossier: true, onParcel: (p) => console.log(p.properties.parcel_id) }); If the dossier is not available, the popup falls back to the basic parcel data.
data.routecontrol#RouteControl:
A route planner: click start and destination, switch the profile, see distance and time, up to two alternatives for cars.
const route = new mapx.RouteControl({ profile: "driving-truck", // start profile; default: first of `profiles` profiles: ["driving", "driving-truck", "cycling", "cycling-mtb", "walking"], onRoute: (response, request) => console.log(request.profile, response.routes[0].distance), }); map.addControl(route, "top-right"); await route.setWaypoints([16.3725, 48.2085], [15.3294, 48.2272]); // set both points from code For cars the panel offers avoid tolls and avoid motorways (exclude), for trucks weight, height, width and length. route.last holds the last response. Live example.
data.search-styles-terrain-measuring#Search,: map.addControl(new mapx.SearchControl({ placeholder: "Search" }), "top-left"); // /v1/geocode map.addControl(new mapx.StyleSwitcherControl({ styles: ["streets", "satellite", "outdoors"] }), "top-right"); map.addControl(new mapx.Terrain3DControl(), "top-right"); map.addControl(new mapx.MeasureControl(), "top-right"); // length and area map.addControl(new mapx.ElevationProfileControl(), "top-right"); // draw a line, get the profile

data:
Every helper throws a MapxError when the API answers with an error or the network fails. It mirrors the application/problem+json document of the error catalog.
Property Meaning status HTTP status, 0 for a network error code Stable code such as invalid-parameter, not-found, rate-limited param The offending parameter, if known allowed Accepted values for enumerations detail Explanation for this request retryAfter Seconds to wait on 429 try { await mapx.geocode("Wien", { types: ["village"] }); } catch (e) { if (e instanceof mapx.MapxError && e.code === "invalid-parameter") { console.log(`${e.param} must be one of ${e.allowed.join(", ")}`); } else throw e; } Missing or rejected tokens arrive as 401 (missing-token, invalid-token, token-expired) or 403 (token-blocked, origin-not-allowed, …), see Access and limits. Do not retry them.
Branch on code, never on the text. Send Accept-Language: de through your own fetch if you need German messages; the helpers use the browser default.
data.cancel-stale-requests#Cancel stale reque:
Type-ahead fields should cancel the previous request. A cancelled request throws the browser’s AbortError, not a MapxError:
let ac; input.oninput = async () => { ac?.abort(); ac = new AbortController(); try { show(await mapx.searchSuggest(input.value, { signal: ac.signal })); } catch (e) { if (e.name !== "AbortError") throw e; } };
data.next#Next: Errors and limits with the rate-limit zones SDK helpers
data.retry-with-backoff#Retry with backoff:
Retry only 429, 502, 503 and network errors. Never retry 400, 404 or 422: the same request fails the same way.
async function withRetry(fn, tries = 3) { for (let i = 0; ; i++) { try { return await fn(); } catch (e) { const retryable = e instanceof mapx.MapxError && [0, 429, 502, 503].includes(e.status); if (!retryable || i === tries - 1) throw e; await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, (e.retryAfter ?? 2 ** i) * 1000)); } } } const m = await withRetry(() => mapx.matrix("driving", [[16.3725, 48.2085], [15.3294, 48.2272]]));

/guides/sdk/errors/.title: Errors and retries in the SDK

data: Every helper is a plain async function that returns typed JSON and throws a MapxError on failure. Coordinates are [lng, lat]. Pass signal (an AbortSignal) to cancel a request. All examples run in the browser console on any page that has loaded mapx (install) and set a token with mapx.setAccessToken("YOUR_TOKEN").
data.elevation#Elevation: const h = await mapx.elevation([12.694, 47.074]); // 3726.3 (m), null outside the data const hs = await mapx.elevation([[12.694, 47.074], [12.7, 47.08]], "dsm"); const p = await mapx.elevationProfile([[12.694, 47.074], [12.75, 47.1]], 100); console.log(p.ascent, p.descent, p.min, p.max, p.length);
data.next#Next: Controls and popups Errors and retries SDK reference with all types
data.other-api-host#Other API host: mapx.setApiBase("https://staging.example.com/v1") redirects all helpers, for tests or a mirror.
data.parcels-and-tilequery#Parcels and tilequ: const { features } = await mapx.parcel([15.3294, 48.2272]); // parcel polygon, number, area_m2 const dossier = await mapx.parcelDossier(features[0].properties.parcel_id); // land use, buildings, terrain, addresses, nearest stop const near = await mapx.tilequery(["streets"], [16.3725, 48.2085], { radius: 50, layers: ["road_l"], limit: 3 }); parcel(point, { dossier: true }) returns the dossier for every parcel at the point in one request.
data.routing#Routing:
const vienna = [16.3725, 48.2085], melk = [15.3294, 48.2272]; // All profiles: driving, driving-traffic, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb, walking const car = await mapx.directions("driving", [vienna, melk], { alternatives: true, exclude: ["toll"], annotations: ["duration", "maxspeed"] }); const truck = await mapx.directions("driving-truck", [vienna, melk], { truck: { weight: 40, height: 4, width: 2.55, type: "semi" } }); const mtb = await mapx.directions("cycling-mtb", [vienna, melk], { steps: true, language: "en" }); const bus = await mapx.transitDirections(vienna, [16.4, 48.19], { departAt: "2026-11-09T08:00", routes: 2 }); console.log(car.routes[0].distance, truck.routes[0].truck, mtb.routes[0].legs[0].steps.length); exclude (motorway, toll) works for driving, driving-traffic and driving-truck, truck only for driving-truck. The server validates both: a wrong combination throws a MapxError with code: "bad-request". The ferry exclusion is not part of the typed options yet; use the Directions API for it.
// Reachability and travel times const iso = await mapx.isochrone("cycling", melk, { minutes: [10, 20, 30] }); // GeoJSON polygons const m = await mapx.matrix("driving", [vienna, melk, [14.2858, 48.3069]]); // m.durations[i][j] in seconds // Tour planning: one vehicle, two jobs const tour = await mapx.optimization({ vehicles: [{ id: 1, start: vienna, end: vienna }], services: [{ id: 1, location: melk, service: 300 }, { id: 2, location: [14.2858, 48.3069], service: 300 }], }); console.log(tour.routes[0].steps.map((s) => s.type));
data.search-and-geocoding#Search and geocodin: // Search Box: suggest while typing, retrieve after the click. One session token per search. const sessionToken = crypto.randomUUID(); const hits = await mapx.searchSuggest("Stephansplatz", { sessionToken, proximity: [16.37, 48.21], types: ["poi", "street"], limit: 5 }); const place = await mapx.searchRetrieve(hits[0].mapbox_id, { sessionToken }); // Geocoding, also parcels: "KG 14143 Gst 473/1" const parcels = await mapx.geocode("14143/473/1", { types: ["parcel"], limit: 3 }); // Reverse geocoding: nearest address, street or place const [nearest] = await mapx.reverse([16.3725, 48.2085], { types: ["address"], limit: 1 });
data.static-image-url#Static image URL:
staticImageUrl builds the URL without a request. Use it in , e-mails and PDFs.
const url = mapx.staticImageUrl({ style: "satellite", center: [15.3294, 48.2272], zoom: 17, width: 800, height: 500, format: "webp", retina: true, overlays: [mapx.pin([15.3294, 48.2272], { color: "e11d48", size: "l" })], }); document.querySelector("img").src = url; Use mapx.geojsonOverlay(feature) to draw a polygon (for example a parcel) with Simplestyle properties, and leave center and zoom out to fit the overlays (auto).
data.traffic-transit-weather#Traffic, transit: const bbox = [16.0, 48.0, 16.6, 48.4]; const incidents = await mapx.trafficIncidents({ bbox, active: true, limit: 20 }); // GeoJSON features with text, road, type const near = await mapx.stops({ near: [16.3725, 48.2085], radius: 300, limit: 3 }); const board = await mapx.departures(near[0].id, { limit: 5 }); // scheduled timetable console.log(board.map((d) => `${d.time.slice(11, 16)} ${d.line.name} ${d.headsign}`)); const now = await mapx.weatherCurrent([16.37, 48.2], { limit: 1 }); // nearest station const next = await mapx.weatherForecast([16.37, 48.2], { hours: 6 }); // hourly model values

data:
Pick the endpoint by what the user does.
Task Endpoint Convert a typed address or place to coordinates /v1/geocode Show suggestions while the user types /v1/searchbox/suggest Fill a postal address form /v1/autofill/suggest Check an address /v1/address/validate Find the address at a point /v1/reverse Show places of a kind (pharmacy, station) /v1/searchbox/category/{category} All data is official: the address register, place names, administrative boundaries and cadastre from BEV. Requests are in the search zone, 10 per second and need a token (Access and limits); curl samples send it as a header, browser samples as access_token.
data.batch#Batch: POST /v1/geocode/batch geocodes up to 1000 queries in one request (zone heavy, 30 per minute).
data.geocode-an-address#Geocode an address: const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Herrengasse%2013,%201010%20Wien&types=address&limit=3&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"; const { features } = await (await fetch(url)).json(); const [lon, lat] = features[0].center; Always pass types (address, street, locality, place, district, region, postcode, poi). Narrow the result with bbox=minlon,minlat,maxlon,maxlat or rank by distance with proximity=lon,lat.

data.places-by-category#Places by category: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/searchbox/list/category?language=en" | jq ".listItems[0:3]" curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/searchbox/category/pharmacy?proximity=16.3725,48.2085&limit=5" list/category returns all category IDs with localized names (language=de or en).
data.type-ahead-search#Type-ahead search:
Call suggest on every pause in typing (debounce 200 ms), then retrieve once for the chosen entry. Send the same session_token for both calls.
const token = crypto.randomUUID(); const s = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/searchbox/suggest?q=Stephansdom&proximity=16.3725,48.2085&limit=5&session_token=${token}&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`)).json(); const id = s.suggestions[0].mapbox_id; const r = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/searchbox/retrieve/${id}?session_token=${token}&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`)).json(); const [lon, lat] = r.features[0].geometry.coordinates; Suggestions carry a category (poi_category_ids, for example place_of_worship_church) and the administrative context. Cancel the previous request when a new key is typed (AbortController). Example: Search.

data:
Goal: Run a mapx PMTiles file on your own infrastructure, for example for resilience, internal networks or your own domain, or a subset of it.
Prerequisites: a server, S3-compatible storage or a CDN that supports HTTP range requests. A PMTiles file is a single static file; no tile server is needed.
The files are free to download with a token (Access and limits) at https://tiles.mapx.at/.pmtiles?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN (file names per product under “Key figures” on the product pages). The file name contains the cut-off date and never changes; a new release gets a new name. With attribution under CC BY 4.0 you may redistribute and mirror the files.
Download the file. curl -C - resumes an interrupted download:
curl -C - -O "https://tiles.mapx.at/relief-terrainrgb-20250915-ed2e4341.pmtiles?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN" The orthophoto and the elevation models are very large files; check storage and bandwidth before downloading. For sub-areas step 2 is easier.
Optional: fetch only a subset. With the pmtiles command line tool, extract reads only the tiles of an area from the online file using range requests:
# subset by bounding box (west,south,east,north) pmtiles extract "https://tiles.mapx.at/relief-terrainrgb-20250915-ed2e4341.pmtiles?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN" salzburg.pmtiles --bbox=12.9,47.7,13.2,47.9 # or only up to a zoom level pmtiles extract "https://tiles.mapx.at/relief-terrainrgb-20250915-ed2e4341.pmtiles?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN" overview.pmtiles --maxzoom=12 --bbox=9.5,46.3,17.2,49.1 The output is a complete PMTiles file that you serve like any other.
Serve it. The server must answer Range requests with 206 Partial Content. Example nginx:
location /tiles/ { root /srv; add_header Access-Control-Allow-Origin "*" always; add_header Access-Control-Allow-Headers "Range, If-Match, If-None-Match" always; add_header Access-Control-Expose-Headers "ETag, Content-Length, Content-Range" always; add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"; if ($request_method = OPTIONS) { return 204; } } For S3 and compatible stores, a CORS rule is enough that allows GET and HEAD for your page origin (or *), allows the headers Range, If-Match and If-None-Match, and exposes ETag, Content-Length, Content-Range. Behind a CDN, the CDN must forward range requests to the origin or handle them itself.
Use it in the map. Your own URL instead of tiles.mapx.at:
import { Protocol } from "pmtiles"; maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new Protocol().tile); // source: { type: "raster-dem", url: "pmtiles://https://tiles.example.com/salzburg.pmtiles", tileSize: 512, encoding: "mapbox" } Verify. A range request must return 206 and Content-Range:
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -r 0-16383 https://tiles.example.com/salzburg.pmtiles
data.caching#Caching: Because file names are immutable, set Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable. A new release is published under a new name; your page switches by entering the new URL. Details on caching of the mapx services: Errors, limits and operation.
data.next-steps#Next steps: File format and protocol: PMTiles documentation. Display with MapLibre: First map. Do not forget the credit: Attribution.
data.result#Result:
A file or subset is served independently of mapx, with the same look and accuracy as the original tiles.
An alternative without your own files: the TileJSON address https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/{tileset}.json. It always points to the current release.

data: A static image is one HTTP request that returns a picture. Use it where an interactive map is not possible: PDFs, emails, listings, social previews. The token goes into the URL as access_token, because an image tag cannot send a header. For web pages use a public token (mx_pk_…) with your site as allowed origin; build images for e-mails and PDFs on your server with a secret token (mx_sk_…) so the secret does not end up in the message.
data.aerial-image-for-a-listing#Aerial image:
satellite shows the orthophoto, outdoors adds contours and trails.
https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/satellite/pin-m+ff0000(15.3294,48.2272)/15.3294,48.2272,17/800x600.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN Show the data credit next to the image, see Attribution.
data.fit-a-route-automatically#Fit a route au:
With auto instead of the view, the image shows all overlays.
const dir = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.3294,48.2272?geometries=polyline&overview=simplified&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"; const { routes } = await (await fetch(dir)).json(); const path = encodeURIComponent(routes[0].geometry); // encoded polyline, precision 5 const url = `https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/outdoors/path-5+e11d48(${path})/auto/800x500@2x.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`; The route comes from Directions with geometries=polyline.
data.next#Next: Static Images API Maps: the same styles interactively Parcels: parcel boundary as GeoJSON overlay
data.overlays#Overlays:
Overlays come after the style, separated by commas (up to 50).
Overlay Example Pin pin-s+ff0000(16.3725,48.2085) (size s, m or l, color as hex) Path path-4+1d5bd8-0.8(encodedPolyline) (width, stroke, opacity; polyline precision 5, URL-encoded) GeoJSON geojson({...}) with simplestyle properties (URL-encoded) curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/streets/pin-s+ff0000(16.3725,48.2085)/16.3725,48.2085,14/600x400.png" -o vienna.png
data.raster-tiles-of-a-style#Raster tiles of: For clients that only read raster tiles (Leaflet, QGIS), Static Tiles render a style as 256 or 512 px tiles: /v1/styles/{id}/tiles/{256|512}/{z}/{x}/{y}.
data.url-format#URL format: /v1/static/{style}/{view}/{width}x{height}[@2x][.png|.webp] /v1/static/{style}/{overlay}/{view}/{width}x{height}... Part Values style streets, streets-dawn, streets-dusk, streets-night, satellite, outdoors view lon,lat,zoom[,bearing] or auto (fits the overlays) size width and height 1 to 1280, up to 2560 with @2x format .png or .webp Images are in the heavy zone (30 per minute). They are cacheable: send If-None-Match and the API answers 304. Cache images on your side and do not request them per page view.

data:
Goal: Build your own, consistently coloured map from the vector tiles of the basemap. mapx provides the data, you decide how it looks.
Prerequisites: a browser, a static web server and a free public token (Access and limits). Basic knowledge of MapLibre styles (sources and layers).
The basemap has 18 layers. This example uses five: landuse_a (land use), water_a (lakes), road_l (roads), building_a (buildings) and boundary_l (boundaries). All layers and fields are in the layer table.
Page and source. The source is the TileJSON link; zoom range and attribution come with it:
<meta charset="utf-8"> <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@4.7.1/dist/maplibre-gl.css"> <script src="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@4.7.1/dist/maplibre-gl.js">script> <style>html, body, #map { margin: 0; height: 100%; }style> <div id="map">div> <script> const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // public token mx_pk_… // adds the token to every request to mapx.at (TileJSON, tiles, fonts) const withToken = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url }); const source = { type: "vector", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/streets.json" }; Background and land use. Every polygon in landuse_a has a kind field (for example forest, farmland, vineyard, alpine_meadow, glacier, rock, residential). One colour per group via a match expression:
const landuse = { id: "landuse", type: "fill", source: "streets", "source-layer": "landuse_a", paint: { "fill-color": ["match", ["get", "kind"], "forest", "#bcd9b0", ["farmland", "vineyard"], "#efe9c8", "alpine_meadow", "#d9e8c4", "glacier", "#f4f8fb", "rock", "#d8d4cf", ["residential", "garden"], "#ebe5de", "#e6e9dc"] } }; Water. Lakes and ponds from water_a as polygons:
const water = { id: "water", type: "fill", source: "streets", "source-layer": "water_a", paint: { "fill-color": "#a9cde8" } }; Roads. road_l has kind: highway, major_road, minor_road, service, track, path. Let widths grow with zoom, draw paths thin and dashed:
const roads = { id: "roads", type: "line", source: "streets", "source-layer": "road_l", filter: ["in", ["get", "kind"], ["literal", ["highway", "major_road", "minor_road", "service"]]], layout: { "line-cap": "round", "line-join": "round" }, paint: { "line-color": ["match", ["get", "kind"], "highway", "#e8a35c", "major_road", "#f0c27a", "#ffffff"], "line-width": ["interpolate", ["exponential", 1.5], ["zoom"], 8, 0.5, 14, 3, 16, 8] } }; const trails = { id: "trails", type: "line", source: "streets", "source-layer": "road_l", minzoom: 13, filter: ["in", ["get", "kind"], ["literal", ["track", "path"]]], paint: { "line-color": "#a07a5a", "line-width": 1, "line-dasharray": [2, 1.5] } }; Buildings. building_a starts at z12 (merged there). From z15 each building has its own outline:
const buildings = { id: "buildings", type: "fill", source: "streets", "source-layer": "building_a", minzoom: 13, paint: { "fill-color": "#cfc7bd", "fill-outline-color": "#a89f94" } }; Boundaries. boundary_l carries kind (country, state, district, municipality). Strong lines for country and state, subtle for municipalities:
const boundaries = [ { id: "b-country", type: "line", source: "streets", "source-layer": "boundary_l", filter: ["==", ["get", "kind"], "country"], paint: { "line-color": "#7a4f8f", "line-width": 1.5 } }, { id: "b-state", type: "line", source: "streets", "source-layer": "boundary_l", filter: ["==", ["get", "kind"], "state"], paint: { "line-color": "#9d86a8", "line-width": 1, "line-dasharray": [4, 2] } }, { id: "b-municipality", type: "line", source: "streets", "source-layer": "boundary_l", minzoom: 10, filter: ["==", ["get", "kind"], "municipality"], paint: { "line-color": "#b9b0be", "line-width": 0.6, "line-dasharray": [2, 2] } } ]; Assemble the map. Order from bottom to top: land use, water, roads, buildings, boundaries.
new maplibregl.Map({ container: "map", transformRequest: withToken, center: [15.334, 48.227], zoom: 14, style: { version: 8, sources: { streets: source }, layers: [ { id: "ground", type: "background", paint: { "background-color": "#f2efe9" } }, landuse, water, roads, trails, buildings, ...boundaries ] } }); </script>
data.labels-and-fonts#Labels and fonts:
For labels (place_p, water_label_p, housenumber_p, road names from road_l via the field name) the style needs a glyphs entry. mapx serves fonts at /v1/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf (list: GET /v1/fonts, for example Open Sans Semibold, Noto Sans Regular). The withToken function from step 1 adds the token to these requests too:
style: { version: 8, glyphs: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf", sources: { streets: source }, layers: [ // ... { id: "places", type: "symbol", source: "streets", "source-layer": "place_p", filter: ["in", ["get", "kind"], ["literal", ["city", "town", "village"]]], layout: { "text-field": ["get", "name"], "text-font": ["Open Sans Semibold"], "text-size": 13 }, paint: { "text-color": "#333", "text-halo-color": "#fff", "text-halo-width": 1.5 } } ] } text-font must be a font that GET /v1/fonts lists.
data.next-steps#Next steps: All layers, fields and values: Basemap. Overlay contour lines and labels: Overlay contour lines. A map for print or as an offline file: Self-host PMTiles.
data.result#Result: A map in your own look: areas by land use, lakes, road network with trails, buildings and administrative boundaries. All data comes from a single tileset.

data:
Traffic data covers the motorway and expressway network (ASFINAG, EVIS.AT) and planned roadworks on other roads. Requests are in the search zone, 10 per second, and need a token (Access and limits); curl samples send it as a header, browser samples as access_token. The map source below takes the token from the transformRequest of First map.
Task Endpoint List incidents, roadworks and closures /v1/traffic/incidents Speed limits on variable message signs /v1/traffic/flow Positions of the signs /v1/traffic/signs Draw traffic on a map /v1/traffic/tiles.json Check whether the data is fresh /v1/traffic/status Route around closures profile driving-traffic
data.incidents-along-a-route#Incidents along:
Pass the route as route (encoded polyline or GeoJSON). Results are sorted by position on the route. For long routes use POST with a JSON body.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -X POST https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "route": { "type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[16.37, 48.21], [16.3, 48.19]] }, "type": "road_closure,construction", "buffer": 50 }' | jq '.total' buffer is the corridor half-width in meters (1 to 1000, default 25).
data.lane-details-on-motorways#Lane details o:
Roadworks on motorways and expressways carry lanes from ASFINAG: one entry per direction and carriageway with the closed lanes (right, middle, left, hard_shoulder), the number of open lanes (open) out of original, contraflow, road_closed and the temporary speed_limit_kmh. direction is aligned (with increasing road kilometers) or opposite. sources lists where a report comes from (evis, asfinag); source names the dataset (evis-planned+asfinag when both match, asfinag-roadworks for roadworks only ASFINAG reports). The text of an EVIS report is never changed.
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?road=A12&type=lane_restriction&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"; const { features } = await (await fetch(url)).json(); for (const f of features) for (const l of f.properties.lanes) console.log(f.properties.road, l.closed, l.open, l.speed_limit_kmh);
data.list-incidents#List incidents:
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?bbox=16.0,48.0,16.8,48.5&type=road_closure,construction&limit=20&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"; const { features, total, next_cursor } = await (await fetch(url)).json(); for (const f of features) console.log(f.properties.road, f.properties.type, f.properties.text); Filters: bbox, road (A1, A 1 and A01 are the same road), road_class (motorway, expressway, federal, state, comma-separated, for A, S, B and L roads), type (accident, congestion, construction, lane_restriction, road_closure, road_hazard, miscellaneous), planned=true|false, and a time window with from and to (UTC). By default only active reports are returned; active=false adds ended and future ones. A report with mandatory: true is binding; show its text unchanged.
Results are sorted by importance: closures and binding reports first, then motorways, expressways, federal and state roads, then by start. Page with limit (default 500, maximum 1000) and cursor: pass next_cursor from the response, or follow next, until next is null. total is the number of matches. Bad values for road, road_class, type or cursor return a 400 problem response.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?road=A1&road_class=motorway&limit=100" | jq '.total, .next'

data.route-with-traffic#Route with traffic: GET /v1/directions/driving-traffic/{coordinates} The route avoids current closures and lists incidents in legs[].incidents. Use incidents=true to get the list with other car profiles.
data.show-traffic-on-the-map#Show traffic on: map.on("load", () => { map.addSource("traffic", { type: "vector", url: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/tiles.json" }); map.addLayer({ id: "traffic", type: "line", source: "traffic", "source-layer": "traffic", paint: { "line-width": 4, "line-color": "#e11d48" } }); }); The style traffic-day already contains the layer. Tiles are in the static zone (5 per second); let the client cache them.

data:
The timetable data covers Austria (ÖBB and the regional transport associations). It is the scheduled timetable: realtime is always false. Requests are in the route zone for journeys and the search zone for stops and departures. Every request needs a token (Access and limits); curl samples send it as a header, browser samples as access_token.
Task Endpoint Find stops near a point /v1/stops Next departures at a stop /v1/departures Journey from A to B /v1/directions/transit/{coordinates}
data.access-by-bike-or-car-bike--ride-park--r:
With access=bike or access=car the first leg is not walked but cycled or driven to a stop. Bikes can be locked at every stop (+2 min); cars park at stops with rail, metro or tram service (+3 min, at most 25 min drive); the algorithm takes the fastest combination, so the station in your own village wins over driving on to the next town if the train is quicker. Official P+R sites from the GIP are added for the car (+2 min, then a walk to the stop). Walking from the start still applies, the minimum counts. The exit is always on foot.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/isochrone/transit/15.16,48.207?contours_minutes=45&depart_at=2026-11-09T07:00&access=car" | jq '.metadata | {access, access_stops_improved, sites: .access_sites[:3]}' Parameter Values Meaning access foot (default), bike, car Mode to the first stop park any (default), official official: bike only at stops within 200 m of a B+R site, car only at official P+R sites sites 1 to 50 (default 10) Entries in metadata.access_sites metadata.access_sites lists the accesses that beat walking, sorted by travel time: source (site for an official P+R, stop for parking at the stop), kind, name, lon, lat, arrive_min (travel time), ready_min (ready to board, incl. parking and walk) and stops_won. Bringing the bike on the train (egress=bike) is not offered: the timetable data carry no bike-carriage information.
data.departure-board#Departure board:
Pass a stop id, or a coordinate to get the departures of all stops around it.
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/departures?stop=at:49:1320&limit=8&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"; const { departures } = await (await fetch(url)).json(); for (const d of departures) console.log(d.time.slice(11, 16), d.line.name, d.headsign, d.platform ?? ""); time is ISO 8601 in Vienna local time. Use time=2026-11-09T08:00 for a later start and horizon (seconds, up to 24 hours) for the window. Outside the timetable period the API answers 422.
data.find-stops#Find stops: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/stops?near=16.3725,48.2085&radius=300&limit=5" | jq '.stops[] | {id, name, modes, lines}' Stops of the same station from different operators are merged and share one id (for example at:49:1320). Use bbox (at most one square degree) to list a map section.
data.journey-planning#Journey planning: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/transit/16.3725,48.2085;16.4202,48.1855?depart_at=2026-11-09T08:00&routes=3" | jq '.routes[0].duration' Pass exactly an origin and a destination. Use depart_at (earliest departure) or arrive_by (latest arrival), default is now. The response contains walking sections on the road network and rides with line, stops and times.
data.next#Next: Transit API Navigation Attribution: timetable data credit
data.reachability-by-transit#Reachability by:
Walking plus public transport as isochrones: profile transit of the isochrone API. The search walks to the stops around the start, rides the scheduled timetable from depart_at and walks on from every stop reached.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/isochrone/transit/16.3725,48.2085?contours_minutes=10,20,30&depart_at=2026-11-10T08:00" | jq '.features[] | {contour: .properties.contour, km2: .properties.area_km2}' Without depart_at the isochrone starts now (Vienna local time). Only contours_minutes applies. The area depends strongly on the time: the same start has a much smaller area at night. Outside the timetable period the API answers 422.
data.show-departures-in-an-app#Show departure: Search a stop with /v1/stops or let the user click the map. Call /v1/departures and refresh every minute. Show line, destination and time; mark missing real-time data with “scheduled”.

Corridor graph: GET /v1/corridor-graph (polyline as polyline6, buffer 100 to 5000 m, profile driving, cycling or walking): compact gzip subgraph of the road network around a route (nodes, directed arcs with travel time and weight, geometry, names, road class, statutory speed limits, turn restrictions) for recomputing a route offline. Speed limits: GET /v1/speedlimits (bbox or corridor as polyline6 plus buffer): statutory GIP limits as compact GeoJSON. Directions: exclude=ferry (all profiles except driving-traffic) and exclude=toll; voice_instructions and banner_instructions also for cycling, cycling-mtb and walking; maxspeed carries legal (false marks a modeled speed that is not a limit). Climate: GET /v1/climate/{lon},{lat} and the section climate in the parcel dossier: solar potential (kWh/m² and sunshine hours per year), temperature and precipitation normals with trend, hot, frost and snow days, drought index SPEI (GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0). Directions: driving and driving-traffic avoid binding closures (EVIS/ASFINAG) and list them in routes[].closures_avoided; exclude also for driving-truck and driving-traffic; voice_instructions and banner_instructions (Mapbox form). Headers Server-Timing, ETag, Last-Modified (styles, TileJSON, OpenAPI; conditional requests answer 304) and RateLimit-Policy per endpoint group. data.epsg4326-and-epsg3857#EPSG:4326 and EPSG:
EPSG:4326 (WGS84) EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator) Unit degrees metres Used for input and output of the APIs, GeoJSON, GPS tile scheme of maps Example 12.694, 47.074 1413090, 5954161 Inputs to the APIs are always WGS84 (EPSG:4326). Tiles are in Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), see Tile scheme. Clients convert between them themselves; you do not need to compute tile coordinates.
Web Mercator distances in Austria are about 50 % larger than true metres (factor 1 / cos(latitude)). Do not measure lengths and areas in EPSG:3857; use geodesic measurement or a local system such as EPSG:31287 (MGI / Austria Lambert) or EPSG:3035 (ETRS89-LAEA).
data.official-sources-mgi-and-etrs89#Official:
The authorities’ source data uses different systems: Austrian national survey (MGI, for example Gauss-Krüger M28/M31/M34 and Lambert) and ETRS89 (for example ETRS89-LAEA, UTM). Between MGI and WGS84/ETRS89 there is a positional offset of several metres that is corrected with an official transformation grid.
mapx transforms correctly: all products are converted to WGS84 and Web Mercator with the official transformation procedure. You get layers that line up without applying a transformation yourself. When you overlay your own official data in MGI, use the transformation grid of your software (for example QGIS with the BEV grid), otherwise it shifts by a few metres.
data.order-longitude-first#Order: longitude f:
All mapx interfaces, TileJSON, MapLibre and GeoJSON use lon, lat (longitude, then latitude), that is east-west before north-south:
12.694,47.074 // lon,lat: Großglockner area Many map apps and GPS devices show lat, lon instead. Swapped values end up in the Indian Ocean, not in Austria. The elevation API expects points=lon,lat;lon,lat. Leaflet takes [lat, lon] in L.latLng, MapLibre and OpenLayers [lon, lat].

data: Terrain-RGB stores one elevation per pixel in the three color channels of an image. This lets elevation tiles be served in ordinary image formats, and clients such as MapLibre compute shading and 3D terrain from them.
data.decoding#Decoding: const hoehe = (r, g, b) => -10000 + (r * 65536 + g * 256 + b) * 0.1; hoehe = -10000 + (r.astype("uint32") * 65536 + g * 256 + b) * 0.1 # r, g, b als numpy-Arrays
data.formula#Formula: height_m = -10000 + (R · 65536 + G · 256 + B) · 0.1 R is the most significant byte. The value q = R·65536 + G·256 + B lies between 0 and 16,777,215, so the elevation lies between −10,000 m and +1,667,721.5 m in steps of 0.1 m.
data.what-to-watch-for#What to watch for: Read the image format losslessly. mapx serves lossless WebP. Any lossy intermediate step (JPEG, color profile, premultiplied alpha, scaling while decoding) distorts the elevation. Do not interpolate before decoding. Blending RGB values does not give a blended elevation. Decode first, then average. Mapbox-compatible. encoding: "mapbox" in MapLibre. Terrarium (R·256 + G + B/256 − 32768) is a different encoding and is not served by mapx. 512 pixels, no border. tileSize: 512. Application: DTM terrain model.

data: All mapx tiles follow the common web map scheme. With MapLibre, Leaflet, OpenLayers or QGIS you do not need to configure anything; for your own requests and calculations, here is what matters.
data.512-pixel-tiles#512-pixel tiles:
mapx raster tiles (elevation models, orthophoto) are 512 × 512 pixels, not 256. A 512 tile covers the same area as four 256 tiles one level deeper. Clients need the right setting:
MapLibre: tileSize: 512 (automatic with TileJSON). Leaflet: tileSize: 512, zoomOffset: -1. OpenLayers: tileSize: 512 on the source. QGIS: tile resolution 512. If you forget it, the map looks off by one zoom level and blurry or too fine.
data.further-reading#Further reading: Elevation values in tiles: Terrain-RGB. Coordinates and projections: Coordinates.
data.overzoom#Overzoom:
If a level is higher than the stored one, the client scales up the tiles of the highest level (overzoom). The image does not get sharper, but the map stays usable. In MapLibre set maxzoom of the source to the highest existing level (automatic from TileJSON); the map itself may zoom further. Requests outside the zoom range return 404, see Errors and limits.
Vector tiles are not redrawn on overzoom; the geometry of the highest level is stretched. For the cadastre (z16 only) set minzoom: 16 in the style.
data.projection-and-address#Projection and ad:
The world is projected in Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) onto a square and divided into zoom levels. At level z the square has 2^z × 2^z tiles. A tile is addressed as z/x/y: x counts from west to east, y from north to south (XYZ scheme, not TMS), both starting at 0.
Tile for a point lon, lat (degrees) at level z:
function tile(lon, lat, z) { const n = 2 ** z; const x = Math.floor(((lon + 180) / 360) * n); const r = (lat * Math.PI) / 180; const y = Math.floor(((1 - Math.log(Math.tan(r) + 1 / Math.cos(r)) / Math.PI) / 2) * n); return { z, x, y }; } tile(12.694, 47.074, 12); // { z: 12, x: 2192, y: 1439 } A tile is served by https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/{tileset}/{z}/{x}/{y}.{ext}, see Tiles.
data.resolution-per-zoom-level#Resolution per:
Resolution depends on latitude. The table applies to 47.5° N, the middle of Austria:
Zoom m per pixel Tile edge (km) Note z5 1,652 846 z6 826 423 z7 413 212 z8 207 106 z9 103 53 z10 52 26 z11 26 13 z12 13 6.61 z13 6.46 3.30 z14 3.23 1.65 z15 1.61 0.83 z16 0.81 0.41 highest stored level (≈ 1 m source) z17 0.40 0.21 overzoom (client) One level deeper halves the pixel size. The elevation models exist up to z16, the orthophoto up to z18.

data.attribution#Attribution: Show the source of the data wherever the map or result is visible. MapLibre adds the text for you when you load a style or TileJSON. See Attribution.
data.cors-and-caching#CORS and caching: CORS allows every origin, so you can call the APIs straight from the browser. The preflight answer of the API does not list the Authorization header yet, so in browser code send the token as access_token in the URL. Responses without a token in the URL are cacheable by shared caches; responses that contain your token (styles requested with access_token) are private.
data.get-a-token#Get a token:
All endpoints under https://api.mapx.at/v1/, https://routing.mapx.at/, https://search.mapx.at/ and all tiles under https://tiles.mapx.at/ need a token. It is free and there is no usage-based charge.
Open account.mapx.at and register with your e-mail address (an 8-digit code is sent to you) or sign in with Google or Microsoft. You must agree to be contacted about the service and your account (security, changes, shutdown). Marketing mail is a separate, optional checkbox. Under Tokens create as many named tokens as you like. The token is shown once; copy it then. You can block, rotate or delete a token at any time, deleting takes effect immediately. Send the token with every request (see below). The Usage page shows requests per token, product and day, including rejected requests with the reason. The OpenAPI description https://api.mapx.at/v1/openapi.json and CORS preflight requests (OPTIONS) work without a token.
data.next#Next: First map in 5 minutes Errors and limits
data.rate-limits#Rate limits:
Limits apply per token and zone (requests without a valid token count per IP address). Every response carries a RateLimit-Policy header, for example "search";q=10;w=1;burst=30 (10 requests per second plus a burst of 30). Exceeding a limit returns 429 with Retry-After. On top of the zones a token may make 6000 requests per minute by default; rejected requests with rate-limited are counted.
Zone Requests Used by tiles 100/s, burst 200 tiles, TileJSON, glyphs, sprites search 10/s, burst 30 geocoding, Search Box, autofill, tilequery, parcel, departures, weather, traffic route 5/s, burst 20 directions, transit journeys elevation 10/s, burst 20 elevation and profile static 5/s, burst 60 Static Tiles, traffic tiles heavy 30/min, burst 5 static images, isochrone, matrix, matching, optimization, batch geocoding For bulk work, download the PMTiles file once instead of requesting millions of tiles. Details and retry advice: Errors and limits.
data.send-the-token#Send the token:
Use the header in server code and scripts. In the browser use the query parameter: images and MapLibre tile URLs cannot set headers, and the CORS preflight does not allow the Authorization header.
# header curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Melk&limit=1" | jq # query parameter curl -s "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Melk&limit=1&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN" | jq const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Melk&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"); // in the browser use access_token; Node can use the header Maps with MapLibre GL JS. The simplest way is a transformRequest that adds the token to every request to mapx.at, never to other hosts:
const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // public token mx_pk_… const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: "map", style: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets", transformRequest: (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url, }), }); When you request a style with ?access_token=…, the API writes the token into all mapx.at URLs of the style (tiles, glyphs, sprites). Clients that cannot set transformRequest then work with style: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN". Such a response is private and must not be shared.
With the SDK. mapx.map({ accessToken: "YOUR_TOKEN", … }) or mapx.setAccessToken("YOUR_TOKEN") once; all helpers, styles, tiles and staticImageUrl() then carry the token. See SDK.
PMTiles files. Append the token to the file URL: pmtiles://https://tiles.mapx.at/.pmtiles?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN.
Android. Send Authorization: Bearer plus X-Mapx-Android-Package (package name) and X-Mapx-Android-Cert (SHA-256 of the signing certificate, read at run time with PackageManager).
Without a valid token the API answers 401 (missing-token, invalid-token, token-expired) or 403 (token-blocked, pk-not-allowed, origin-missing, origin-not-allowed, app-not-allowed, ip-not-allowed) as application/problem+json; see Errors and limits. During the transition period the token may still be optional: requests without one succeed and carry the header X-Mapx-Token-Warning.
data.two-kinds-of-token#Two kinds of token: Kind Prefix Use Restrictions Public mx_pk_… Websites and apps. The token is visible in the page source or in the APK, so it only works where you allow it. Read-only products, GET/HEAD only. Bound to allowed origins (for example https://example.com, *.example.com) or to an Android app (package name plus SHA-256 of the signing certificate). Secret mx_sk_… Servers, scripts and CI. Never put it into a web page or an app. No origin binding; optionally bound to IP ranges (CIDR). A public token is checked against the Origin header (for tiles and images without one, against the Referer host). Requests from other sites get 403 with the reason origin-not-allowed. Add localhost to the origins only while you develop.

data.can-i-use-the-maps-offline#Can I use the: Yes. Download a PMTiles file and serve it yourself: Self-host PMTiles, QGIS.
data.do-i-need-a-token-or-an-account#Do I nee: Yes, a free account and API token. Register at account.mapx.at, create a token and send it as Authorization: Bearer (servers) or access_token (browsers, images). CORS is open. See Access and limits.
data.does-a-url-change-when-there-is-new-data: API URLs (/v1/tiles/streets/..., TileJSON) stay the same. PMTiles file names contain the date, so old files stay valid. Use the TileJSON to always get the current file.
data.how-current-is-the-data#How current is t: Each tileset has a source date, shown on its page under Tilesets and in the stand field of GET /v1/tiles.
data.is-the-cadastre-legally-binding#Is the c: No. It shows parcel boundaries for orientation and does not replace a land register extract or a survey.
data.is-there-data-outside-austria#Is there d: Austria only. Orthophoto and base map reach a little into neighboring countries at the border.
data.may-i-use-it-commercially#May I use it c: Yes. The data is licensed CC BY 4.0: name the source, everything else is free.
data.my-map-is-blurry#My map is blurry: Raster tiles are 512 px. Set tileSize: 512 in your client. See Tile scheme.
data.my-points-land-in-the-wrong-country#My p: Longitude and latitude are swapped. mapx and GeoJSON use lon,lat. See Coordinates.
data.what-does-it-cost#What does it cost?: Nothing. Rate limits apply per token and zone.
data.what-is-the-difference-between-dtm-and-d: The DTM is bare ground, the DSM includes trees and buildings. Use the DTM for gradients and profiles, the DSM for visibility and building heights. See Elevation.
data.where-do-i-report-a-problem#Where do I r: Write to support@mapx.at (technical questions and bugs) or info@mapx.at (everything else).
data.which-old-names-still-work#Which old nam: The former German style, tileset and category names work until 2027-05-31. See Migration.
data.why-do-i-get-401-or-403#Why do I get 401: 401 means the token is missing, invalid or expired. 403 means it is blocked, or a public token is used from an origin or app that is not allowed (origin-not-allowed). The code in the error body names the reason. See Access and limits.
data.why-do-i-get-404-for-a-tile#Why do I get: The tile lies outside the data area or zoom range, the extension does not match the type (pbf vector, webp raster) or the tileset name is wrong. Treat 404 as an empty tile.
data.why-do-i-get-429#Why do I get 429?: You exceeded the rate limit of the zone. Wait Retry-After seconds and retry with growing delay. For heavy loads use PMTiles.

Coordinates are always lon,lat, separated by ;.

data:
Annotation. Extra values per route segment, for example speed or elevation. Requested with annotations.
Cadastral municipality (KG). Austrian land registry unit. A parcel number is only unique within one KG.
Contours. Lines of equal elevation. Tileset contours.
DEM. Digital elevation model, here stored as Terrain-RGB tiles. See Terrain-RGB.
DSM / DTM. Digital surface model (including buildings and trees) and digital terrain model (bare ground).
Geocoding. Turning an address or place name into coordinates. Reverse geocoding does the opposite.
Glyphs. Font data that MapLibre loads to draw labels. See Styles API.
Isochrone. An area reachable from a point within a given time or distance.
Orthophoto. Rectified aerial photograph.
PMTiles. Single-file archive of tiles, read with HTTP range requests. Every tileset is available as one.
Profile. The kind of traveler for routing: driving, driving-truck, cycling, walking.
Sprite. Image atlas with the icons of a style.
Style. A JSON document that tells the map which data to draw and how. mapx offers streets, satellite and outdoors.
Tile. A square piece of map addressed as {z}/{x}/{y}. See Tile scheme.
TileJSON. A small JSON description of a tileset: URL template, zoom range, bounds, attribution.
Tileset. A named collection of tiles, for example streets or cadastre. See Tilesets.

mapx is a set of maps and location APIs for Austria. All data comes from official open sources (BEV, GIP.at, ASFINAG, GeoSphere Austria, ÖBB and others), so there is no usage-based pricing. A free account and API token are required (Access and limits).
Product What you get Start Maps Vector and raster tiles, ready-made styles (streets, satellite, outdoors), TileJSON Maps Search Geocoding, type-ahead Search Box, address autofill and validation Search Navigation Routes for car, truck, bike and foot, isochrones, matrices, map matching, tolls Navigation Traffic Incident reports, motorway speed limits, a traffic layer Traffic Transit Public transport journeys, stops, departures Transit Static images PNG or WebP maps with pins, paths and GeoJSON Static images Elevation and terrain Heights, elevation profiles, terrain and surface models Elevation Parcels Cadastral parcel with area and number at any point Parcels The APIs follow the conventions of well-known web mapping services: the same URL shapes, GeoJSON responses and MapLibre-compatible styles. Existing MapLibre, Leaflet or OpenLayers code needs few changes.

Each tileset is available as TileJSON and XYZ tiles through the Tiles API and as one immutable PMTiles file (the source date is part of the file name). All data is licensed CC BY 4.0, see Attribution.

Use a tileset by name:

Alternatively open the PMTiles file directly as a layer (QGIS 3.32 and later reads PMTiles over HTTP). curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/cadastre.json curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -o kachel.pbf https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/cadastre/14/8860/5730.pbf Because only z16 exists, set minzoom: 16 in the style; the source with maxzoom: 16 overzooms automatically.

data.index-and-date-overlays#Index and date o:
Four further fixed tilesets are derived from the same composite. They are transparent where there is no value, so they work as overlays on sentinel2, a satellite image or a street map. All are WebP, 512 px, z5 to z13, same attribution; each is replaced daily together with sentinel2. They appear in /v1/tiles only once the file exists. The TileJSON carries the value range and colour ramp in mapx:legend.
Tileset Shows Value and colour sentinel2-datum Acquisition date per pixel age in days before mapx:stand: 0 green, 20 yellow, 45 orange, 90 red, 180 dark red sentinel2-ndvi Vegetation, (NIR - red) / (NIR + red) -0.1 grey, 0.05 bare, 0.2 sand, 0.4 light green, 0.85 dark green sentinel2-ndwi Water, (green - NIR) / (green + NIR) only values above 0: light blue (0) to dark blue (0.7) sentinel2-ndsi Snow, (green - SWIR) / (green + SWIR) only values from 0.4: light blue to white (0.8); water is excluded by a NIR threshold map.addSource("ndvi", { type: "raster", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/sentinel2-ndvi.json", tileSize: 512 }); map.addLayer({ id: "ndvi", type: "raster", source: "ndvi", paint: { "raster-opacity": 0.8 } }); In the mapx viewer they are the overlays “Acquisition date”, “Vegetation (NDVI)”, “Water (NDWI)” and “Snow (NDSI)” in the layer group Satellite, with legend and opacity slider.
data.notes#Notes: The image mixes several days (the date is stored per pixel); dense ground fog lasting weeks can remain despite the filter. 10 m source resolution: z13 is the last level with real gain in detail.
data.source-and-method#Source and method: Source: Sentinel-2 L2A (surface reflectance) from ESA/Copernicus as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF via Element84 Earth Search (STAC, AWS Open Data). Only bands B04, B03, B02 (10 m) and the scene classification SCL (20 m) are read, with HTTP range requests. Mask: SCL classes 4 (vegetation), 5 (bare soil), 6 (water) and 11 (snow) are valid; clouds, shadows, cirrus, dark and unclassified pixels do not count. The mask is eroded by 40 m, and pixels with a very high blue share (haze) are dropped, except snow. Robust value instead of latest value: each pixel keeps its last 5 valid observations. The output is a value of medium brightness among the observations of the 45 days before the most recent one; outliers (too blue, too bright, too dark) against the median are discarded. The image stays current while haze and thin clouds drop out. Gaps: older observations fill pixels that were never clear recently; remaining holes are filled from neighbouring pixels. Seams: each scene is brightness-matched to the stored data, and edges between acquisition days are blended softly.
