data.add-to-your-map#Add to your map: MapLibreQGISPythoncurl import * as maplibregl from "maplibre-gl"; maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: "map", center: [12.694, 47.074], zoom: 11, pitch: 60, style: { version: 8, sources: { dem: { type: "raster-dem", url: "pmtiles://https://tiles.mapx.at/relief-terrainrgb-20250915-ed2e4341.pmtiles?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN", tileSize: 512, encoding: "mapbox", maxzoom: 16 } }, terrain: { source: "dem", exaggeration: 1.2 }, layers: [{ id: "hill", type: "hillshade", source: "dem" }] } }); map.on("click", (e) => console.log(map.queryTerrainElevation(e.lngLat))); In the Browser panel, right-click XYZ Tiles, New Connection. URL https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN, Min. Zoom 5, Max. Zoom 16, tile resolution 512. The layer shows the raw tiles (encoded color). Elevations follow from the formula in “Encoding” ((R*65536 + G*256 + B)*0.1 - 10000), for example in the Raster Calculator on the three bands. # pip install pmtiles pillow numpy requests from PIL import Image from pmtiles.reader import Reader URL = "https://tiles.mapx.at/relief-terrainrgb-20250915-ed2e4341.pmtiles?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN" def get_bytes(offset, length): r = requests.get(URL, headers={"Range": f"bytes={offset}-{offset + length - 1}"}, timeout=30) r.raise_for_status() return r.content reader = Reader(get_bytes) tile = reader.get(12, 2192, 1439) # z, x, y (Grossglockner) rgb = np.asarray(Image.open(io.BytesIO(tile)).convert("RGB")).astype(np.uint32) hoehe = -10000 + (rgb[..., 0] * 65536 + rgb[..., 1] * 256 + rgb[..., 2]) * 0.1 print(hoehe.shape, hoehe.min(), hoehe.max()) # one tile via the XYZ endpoint curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -o kachel.webp https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb/12/2192/1439.webp # whole file, resumable curl -C - -O "https://tiles.mapx.at/relief-terrainrgb-20250915-ed2e4341.pmtiles?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"
data.attribution#Attribution:
Required under CC BY 4.0. Text:
Relief: BEV – ALS-DTM 1 m (reference date 15 Sep 2025), CC BY 4.0 HTML (as in the PMTiles metadata; MapLibre picks it up automatically from the tileset):
Relief: <a href="https://data.bev.gv.at/geonetwork/srv/ger/catalog.search#/metadata/5ce253fc-b7c5-4362-97af-6556c18a45d9">BEV – ALS-DTM 1 ma> (Stichtag 15.09.2025), CC BY 4.0 More: License.
data.encoding#Encoding: height_m = -10000 + (R · 65536 + G · 256 + B) · 0.1 Theoretical value range −10000 m to +1,667,721.5 m in steps of 0.1 m; in Austria the values lie between about 115 m (Lake Neusiedl) and about 3,798 m (Grossglockner). Values are rounded to 0.1 m when written (round half to even at exactly .5, see Rust code above); values outside the range are clamped. WebP lossless: lossy compression would directly corrupt the encoded elevations. Do not use alpha information; read the RGB bands unchanged (no color management, no premultiplied alpha). 512 × 512 pixels, no border (no 1 px skirt). In MapLibre specify tileSize: 512 and encoding: "mapbox". In detail: Terrain-RGB.
data.horizontal-resolution-by-zoom#Horizontal:
At 47.5° N, 512 px tiles, Web Mercator:
Zoom m per pixel Tile edge (km) Note z5 1,652 846 z6 826 423 z7 413 212 z8 207 106 z9 103 53 z10 52 26 z11 26 13 z12 13 6.61 z13 6.46 3.30 z14 3.23 1.65 z15 1.61 0.83 z16 0.81 0.41 highest stored level (≈ 1 m source) z17 0.40 0.21 overzoom (client) The data come from a 1 m raster. z16 (about 0.8 m per pixel) is the finest level and preserves the resolution of the source. There are no tiles above z16: from z17 MapLibre scales up the z16 tile (set maxzoom: 16).
data.live-map#Live map: BEV – ALS-DTM 1 m (Stichtag 15.09.2025), CC BY 4.0"> 3D terrain Hillshade Click the map: elevation and tile RGB. This map requires JavaScript. Clicking reads the tile of the current zoom level (z16 at most) via range request, decodes the pixel at the click point with the formula under “Encoding” and shows elevation and RGB value. With 3D enabled, the value of queryTerrainElevation is shown as well.
data.notes#Notes: Quantization 0.1 m. The deviation from the source is within the rounding range. Vertical accuracy per BEV ± 0.50 m, see Vertical resolution and accuracy. The DTM shows the terrain without buildings, trees and bridges. For the surface there is the DSM. Coverage is the rectangle 9.53–17.17° E, 46.37–49.02° N. Outside Austria and in gaps the value is a smooth continuation of the terrain, not a measurement.
data.source-and-currency#Source and currency:
The DTM is derived from the BEV ALS-DTM 1 m (airborne laser scanning, terrain only). The reference date is in the specifications and the file name; a file never changes, a new release is a new file.
Source: BEV (Austrian Federal Office of Metrology and Surveying), reference date 15 Sep 2025.
data.specifications#Specifications: Tilesetrelief-terrainrgb File relief-terrainrgb-20250915-ed2e4341.pmtiles Reference date 2025-09-15 Format webp, encoding mapbox, 512 px Zoom levels z5–z16 Bounds (WGS84) 9.5306 / 46.3697 / 17.1661 / 49.0235 (W/S/O/N) Vertical resolution 0.1 m (Terrain-RGB) Vertical accuracy (source) ± 0.50 m per BEV, larger in high mountains Height reference EVRF2000 Austria, orthometric (EPSG:9274) License CC BY 4.0
data.vertical-resolution-and-accuracy#Vertica:
Value Meaning Vertical resolution 0.1 m smallest height step of the encoding Deviation from source ≤ 0.05 m rounding during encoding, otherwise unchanged (lossless) Vertical accuracy of the source ± 0.50 m stated by BEV for the ALS-DTM; larger deviations are possible in high mountains Height reference EVRF2000 Austria orthometric heights (EPSG:9274), as in the source The encoding is five times finer than the accuracy of the survey, so it does not limit quality.
In the overview levels z15 to z5 each pixel is the mean of the finer level. The vertical resolution stays 0.1 m, but small peaks and summits are smoothed. For exact point heights read z16 or use the elevation API.

data:
All requests need a token (Access and limits); in server code use a secret token (mx_sk_…) and never ship it in a web page.
Fleet and delivery software needs a route that a truck can really drive, travel times for many pairs, a good order of stops and the current traffic situation. All four are one request each. Coordinates are lon,lat, times are seconds, distances metres.

data.plan-the-tour#Plan the tour:
POST /v1/optimization assigns jobs to vehicles and orders them: capacity, time windows, service times (seconds), start and end per vehicle. At most 10 vehicles, 50 jobs and 60 distinct locations per request.
const body = { profile: "driving", vehicles: [{ id: 1, start: [16.3725, 48.2083], end: [16.3725, 48.2083], time_window: [28800, 61200] }], services: [ { id: 1, location: [15.6256, 48.2049], service: 300, time_windows: [[32400, 43200]] }, { id: 2, location: [14.2858, 48.3069], service: 600 }, ], }; const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/optimization?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN", { method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(body) }); const tour = await res.json(); console.log(tour.routes[0].steps.map((s) => s.id ?? s.type), tour.unassigned); // unassigned: jobs that did not fit Draw the result with one directions request through tour.routes[0].steps locations (up to 25 points); see the tour planning example.
data.traffic#Traffic:
Use driving-traffic for a route with the current traffic and closures. Incidents on the route come with incidents=true in legs[].incidents. For a region, list the active incidents or show the traffic style:
const bbox = [14.5, 47.8, 16.9, 48.6]; // Lower Austria const { features } = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?bbox=${bbox}&active=true&type=construction&limit=50&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`)).json(); console.log(features.length, features[0]?.properties.road, features[0]?.properties.text); The map style traffic-day shows the flow; see the example. Traffic data: ASFINAG / EVIS.AT (CC BY 4.0).
data.travel-times-for-many-pairs#Travel times:
matrix answers all pairs in one request, up to the limits of the Matrix API. Use sources and destinations (indices) to ask for one row only.
const depots = [[16.3725, 48.2085], [15.3294, 48.2272], [14.2858, 48.3069]]; const q = depots.map((p) => p.join(",")).join(";"); const m = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/matrix/driving/${q}?annotations=duration,distance&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`)).json(); console.log(m.durations[0][1] / 60, "min", m.distances[0][1] / 1000, "km"); // Vienna to Melk
data.truck-routes#Truck routes:
The profile driving-truck takes the vehicle size and avoids roads with matching weight, height, width and length limits and bans. Without parameters it assumes 40 t, 4 m high and 2.55 m wide.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving-truck/15.6256,48.2049;15.3294,48.2272?weight=40&height=4&width=2.55&length=16.5&truck_type=semi&overview=false" \ | jq '.routes[0] | {distance, duration, truck, toll_go_km: .toll.truck_go_km}' routes[0].toll.truck_go_km is the length subject to the GO toll; per step it is truck_go_m. Speeds follow truck limits (80 km/h on motorways). District-wide bans from free-text ordinances are not routed: affected roads come as steps[].notices[] with type: "truck_restriction"; show them to the dispatcher. For cars, exclude=toll and exclude=motorway avoid toll sections and motorways (profiles driving, driving-traffic and driving-truck); exclude=ferry works for every profile except driving-traffic.
With the SDK:
const r = await mapx.directions("driving-truck", [[15.6256, 48.2049], [15.3294, 48.2272]], { truck: { weight: 40, height: 4, width: 2.55, length: 16.5, type: "semi" }, steps: true }); const notices = r.routes[0].legs.flatMap((l) => l.steps).flatMap((s) => s.notices ?? []);

data: Municipal tools work with parcels and addresses and need to be understood by residents. mapx is free with an API token (Access and limits); snippets that use mapx.… expect mapx.setAccessToken("YOUR_TOKEN") once, or accessToken in mapx.map. The pieces below combine the cadastre, the address register, the timetable and the map for the web page of a municipality.
data.check-addresses#Check addresses:
Forms for registrations, applications and reports should accept only existing addresses. address/validate compares the input with the address register and returns match, corrected, ambiguous or not_found with the corrected address and coordinates.
const q = new URLSearchParams({ street: "Haubtplatz", housenumber: "1", postcode: "3390", place: "Melk" }); const r = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/address/validate?${q}&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`)).json(); console.log(r.status, r.deviations.map((d) => `${d.field}: ${d.input} > ${d.expected}`), r.address?.full_address ?? r.candidates?.map((c) => c.full_address)); While the person types, offer address autofill; for lists with many addresses use POST /v1/geocode/batch (Search).
data.departures-at-the-town-hall#Departures a:
Residents ask “When does the next bus go?”. The timetable (scheduled, no real-time data) is one request away:
const [stop] = await mapx.stops({ near: [15.3294, 48.2272], radius: 400, limit: 1 }); const board = await mapx.departures(stop.id, { limit: 6 }); document.querySelector("#abfahrten").innerHTML = board.map((d) => ` ${d.time.slice(11, 16)} ${d.line.name} → ${d.headsign} `).join(""); Or add new mapx.DeparturesPopup(map) to a map. See Transit departures and the example. Timetable data: ÖBB-Personenverkehr AG, data source Mobilitätsverbünde Österreich (CC BY 4.0).
data.embed-a-map-in-the-municipal-website#Emb: A map needs one HTML file, MapLibre and the style URL, a free public token and no build (Embed a map). Host the page with your content management system, or embed the file as :
data.next-steps#Next steps: Parcels and Search Transit departures Style the basemap in the colours of your municipality
data.parcels#Parcels:
The cadastre is available as a vector tileset for drawing and as an API for the parcel at a point.
const map = mapx.map({ accessToken: "YOUR_TOKEN", container: "map", style: "satellite-streets", center: [15.3294, 48.2272], zoom: 17 }); new mapx.ParcelPopup(map); // click: number, area, cadastral municipality, buildings Search for a parcel by its number (the cadastral municipality is part of the identity):
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=KG%2014143%20Gst%20473/1&types=parcel&limit=1" | jq '.features[0] | {place_name, center, id: .properties.parcel_id}' The boundaries come from the BEV cadastral map (DKM). The area is computed from the boundary lines and deviates from the register by per mille. State this where the data is shown: for orientation, not legally binding.

data: For a listing you need three things: facts about the parcel, a picture that shows where it lies, and an answer to “how well can I reach it”. All of it comes from official open data (BEV cadastre, orthophoto, GIP, timetables). You need a free API token (Access and limits); the samples show it as YOUR_TOKEN. The data is for orientation and not legally binding.
data.a-picture-for-the-listing#A picture for:
The dossier carries links.static_image: a satellite image with the parcel outline. To build your own, draw the polygon as a GeoJSON overlay and let the image fit it with auto:
const parcel = (await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/parcel/15.3294,48.2272?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN")).json()).features[0]; const outline = { type: "Feature", properties: { stroke: "#e11d48", "stroke-width": 3, fill: "#e11d48", "fill-opacity": 0.2 }, geometry: parcel.geometry }; const img = `https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/satellite/geojson(${encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(outline))})/auto/800x500.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`; document.querySelector("#expose").src = img; // also fine in e-mails and PDFs Use outdoors or streets instead of satellite for a plan view. Add @2x to the size for sharp images on high-resolution screens. See Static images. The image URL contains the token, so use a public token (mx_pk_…) with your site as allowed origin for images on web pages, and render images for e-mails and PDFs on your server with a secret token (mx_sk_…). The image carries the attribution of its data; keep it visible in the layout (Attribution).
data.find-the-parcel#Find the parcel:
Search by parcel number (KG 14143 Gst 473/1, 14143/473/1) or take the parcel at a point, for example from a click or an address:
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Herrengasse%2013,%201010%20Wien&types=address&limit=1" | jq '.features[0].center' curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/parcel/15.3294,48.2272" | jq '.features[0].properties | {parcel_id, parcel_number, area_m2, is_building_land}' curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=KG%2014143%20Gst%20473/1&types=parcel&limit=1" | jq '.features[0].properties.parcel_id'
data.how-well-can-i-reach-it#How well can I r:
Show the area reachable on foot or by bike, and the distance to places that matter.
const here = [15.3294, 48.2272]; const iso = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/isochrone/walking/${here}?contours_minutes=5,10,15&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`)).json(); // GeoJSON polygons const places = [here, [15.3333, 48.2279], [15.3201, 48.2218]]; // address, school, station const m = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/matrix/walking/${places.map((p) => p.join(",")).join(";")}?sources=0`)).json(); console.log(m.durations[0].map((s) => Math.round(s / 60) + " min")); For public transport use the next stop from the dossier and its departures: GET /v1/departures?stop=&limit=5.
curlPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/departures?stop=at:49:1320&limit=3" | jq '.departures[] | {time, line: .line.name, headsign}' import requests r = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/departures", params={"stop": "at:49:1320", "limit": 3}, headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}).json() print([(d["time"][11:16], d["line"]["name"]) for d in r["departures"]])
data.next-steps#Next steps: Parcels and the Parcel on click example Static images with markers and paths Navigation for isochrones and matrices
data.read-the-dossier#Read the dossier:
/v1/parcels/{id} returns everything the open data say about one parcel in a single call: municipality and district, area, land use shares, buildings with heights where the BEV has them, terrain statistics, addresses, the nearest transit stop, the flight year of the orthophoto and a ready-made image link.
const id = "14143-473_1"; // properties.parcel_id from the search or the point query const d = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/parcels/${id}?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`)).json(); const p = d.properties; console.log( `${p.parcel_number} in ${p.cadastral_municipality.name}, ${Math.round(p.area_m2)} m²`, `| buildings: ${p.buildings.count}`, `| ${p.elevation?.min_m}-${p.elevation?.max_m} m, slope ${p.elevation?.slope_mean_deg}°`, `| nearest stop: ${p.nearest_transit_stop?.name} (${p.nearest_transit_stop?.distance_m} m)`, ); Missing data are null or empty lists, never absent. With the SDK: mapx.parcelDossier(id) or mapx.parcel(point, { dossier: true }). For a map click use new mapx.ParcelPopup(map).
data.sun-heat-and-snow-at-the-site#Sun, heat:
Buyers ask for solar yield, summer heat and snow load. /v1/climate/{lon},{lat} answers from GeoSphere Austria data; the same object is properties.climate in the dossier (taken at the inner point of the parcel). Each section names its dataset, grid cell and last day of data.
const c = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/climate/15.3294,48.2272?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN")).json(); console.log( `Global radiation: ${c.solar?.global_radiation_kwh_m2_year} kWh/m² per year, ${c.solar?.sunshine_hours_year} h of sunshine`, `| mean temperature ${c.temperature.mean_annual_c.normal} °C (1991-2020), trend +${c.temperature.trend_c_per_decade} °C per decade`, `| hot days (TX ≥ 30 °C): ${c.temperature_extremes.hot_days_per_year.normal} → ${c.temperature_extremes.hot_days_per_year.recent} per year`, `| snow days: ${c.snow.snow_days_per_winter.normal} per winter, now ${c.snow.current.depth_cm} cm`, `| drought (SPEI 365): ${c.drought.spei365.class}`, ); A rough photovoltaic estimate is the radiation on the roof times the module efficiency and a performance ratio (about 0.8); the value is for orientation and replaces no yield study. The first request for an area that nobody has asked for can take up to 20 seconds, later ones answer from a cache. In the dossier the section is null with status: "partial" until the data are loaded; ask again after retry_after_s. Reference: Climate API. Show the credit: GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0 (Attribution).

data:
The snippets that use mapx.… expect mapx.setAccessToken("YOUR_TOKEN") once (Access and limits).
Visitors ask “Which way by bike, how steep is it, and what is the weather?”. The answers come from the same API: routes with the profiles cycling and cycling-mtb, a profile of the heights, the signposted cycle routes on the map and the forecast for the destination.
data.elevation-profile#Elevation profile:
Every tour page benefits from a profile. Feed the route geometry (2 to 512 points; the default simplified route geometry fits) into the elevation API:
const route = (await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/cycling/15.3294,48.2272;15.6141,48.4097?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN")).json()).routes[0]; // the default overview=simplified keeps the line below the 512-point limit const p = await mapx.elevationProfile(route.geometry.coordinates, 120); console.log(`up ${Math.round(p.ascent)} m, down ${Math.round(p.descent)} m, ${Math.round(p.min)}-${Math.round(p.max)} m`); // p.distances[i] (m from start) and p.elevations[i] (m) give the chart The height model is the official DTM of the BEV. See Elevation profile for a finished chart and the live example.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Navigation and Elevation and terrain 3D terrain for a spectacular tour map Static images for brochures and newsletters
data.reachability-for-the-area#Reachability f:
Which destinations can guests reach in 30 minutes by bike? One isochrone request:
const iso = await mapx.isochrone("cycling", [15.3294, 48.2272], { minutes: [15, 30, 45] }); // largest area first map.addSource("reach", { type: "geojson", data: iso }); map.addLayer({ id: "reach", type: "fill", source: "reach", paint: { "fill-color": "#2346d8", "fill-opacity": 0.12 } }); For public transport to the trailhead use transitDirections with bike: true to ride to the stop.
data.routes-for-bikes#Routes for bikes:
cycling prefers cycle paths and signposted routes and rates unpaved sections and steep grades worse. cycling-mtb prefers forest tracks and singletrails. With steps=true every step carries the type of infrastructure and the surface, routes[].summary has ascent, descent and maximum grade.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/cycling-mtb/15.3294,48.2272;15.4,48.3?steps=true&overview=false" \ | jq '.routes[0] | {distance, duration, summary}' const r = await mapx.directions("cycling", [[15.3294, 48.2272], [15.6141, 48.4097]], { steps: true, alternatives: true, annotations: ["elevation"] }); console.log(r.routes.map((x) => `${(x.distance / 1000).toFixed(1)} km, up ${x.summary?.ascent_m} m`));
data.show-the-cycle-routes#Show the cycle rou:
The streets style contains the signposted cycle and MTB routes as the layer group bike_routes. Switch it on with the style metadata, or let the user toggle it:
const map = mapx.map({ accessToken: "YOUR_TOKEN", container: "map", style: "streets", center: [15.45, 48.3], zoom: 10 }); map.addControl(new mapx.LayerControl({ groups: ["bike_routes", "relief"] }), "top-right"); map.addControl(new mapx.RouteControl({ profiles: ["cycling", "cycling-mtb", "walking"] }), "top-right"); The SDK example shows both controls together.
data.weather-for-the-destination#Weather for: const f = await mapx.weatherForecast([12.694, 47.074], { hours: 12 }); // Grossglockner console.log(f.hours.map((h) => `${h.time.slice(11, 16)} ${h.temperature_c}°C ${h.precipitation_mm} mm`).join("\n")); weatherCurrent gives the measurements of the nearest stations. As a map layer see the weather overlay. Weather data: GeoSphere Austria (CC BY 4.0).
